jurisdiction.name: Luxembourg
jurisdiction.creation: The Law of 5 August 2005 on financial collateral arrangements, as amended, most recently by the laws of 20 July 2022 and 15 July 2024, governs the whole field. Collateral means financial instruments and claims, and financial instruments is given the broadest possible meaning, expressly including shares, units in collective investment undertakings, bonds and certificates of deposit. A pledge is created by agreement; the provision of collateral must be capable of being evidenced in writing, in electronic or other durable form, and must allow the collateral to be identified, and for book-entry financial instruments and cash claims it is enough to show that they have been credited to, or form a credit in, a designated account. Article 4 allows the parties to agree an all-present-and-future pledge without needing to designate the collateral specifically, which is exactly what a revolving portfolio needs. Article 2(4) allows collateral to be provided to a person acting for the account of beneficiaries, a fiduciary or a trustee for determined or determinable third-party beneficiaries, who then enjoy the same rights as direct beneficiaries. The Law also covers title transfer for security purposes and fiduciary transfer under Article 13, where a fiduciary must be a financial sector professional, and repurchase agreements under Articles 15 to 17.
jurisdiction.registration_filing: There is none. Article 26 provides that instruments evidencing a financial collateral arrangement are not subject to registration formalities, and are registered at the fixed rate if voluntarily submitted to the registration formality. There is no equivalent of the English companies charge register for a financial collateral arrangement and no notice filing, which is one of the reasons Luxembourg collateral is quick to take. As in Switzerland, the corollary is that there is nothing to search: priority is determined by the date on which each pledge became enforceable against third parties under Article 5(6). The diligence is therefore documentary, meaning custodian confirmations and express treatment of the custodian's own ranking, rather than a register search.
jurisdiction.perfection_depends_on: Possession, defined functionally through the custodian, is what does the work. Article 5(1) provides that the privilege only remains on the pledged collateral if it has been and remains, or is deemed to have remained, in the possession of the pledgee or an agreed third party. For book-entry financial instruments, Article 5(2)(a) gives four alternatives: simply concluding the pledge agreement, where the pledgee is the custodian; a three-party agreement between provider, pledgee and custodian, or a two-party agreement notified to the custodian, under which the custodian will act on the pledgee's instructions without any further agreement of the provider; booking the instruments to an account of the pledgee; or earmarking them, without number specification, in the custodian's books on an account in the provider's or an agreed third-party custodian's name. The second, third and fourth routes are treated as a waiver by the custodian of its own pledge ranking unless otherwise agreed or notified. For other financial instruments, Article 5(3) requires notification to or acknowledgement by the issuer or the third-party custodian, and for a pledge over claims including cash balances, Article 5(4) makes it effective against the debtor and third parties on the mere conclusion of the pledge contract, although the account debtor can still validly pay the provider until it learns of the pledge. Article 2(3) confirms that a right of substitution, a right to withdraw excess collateral, a right to collect proceeds until further notice, and a reserved right of the provider to give instructions do not prejudice the collateral having been provided, which is a materially more collateral-taker-friendly position than the English dispossession case law.
jurisdiction.enforcement_route: Article 11(1) is the centrepiece: on an enforcement event the pledgee may, unless otherwise provided for and without prior notice, appropriate the pledged collateral or have a third party appropriate it at a price determined before or after appropriation by the agreed valuation method; assign it or cause it to be assigned by private sale in a commercially reasonable manner, on a trading venue on which it is admitted to trading, or by public auction; obtain a judgment attributing the collateral in payment on an expert valuation; net under Part V; appropriate listed financial instruments at the market price, or units in a collective investment undertaking at that price or at the last published net asset value provided it is not more than a year old; request redemption of pledged fund units at the redemption price; or exercise the rights under a pledged insurance contract, including surrender. Article 11(3) obliges a third-party custodian to transfer the instruments to the pledgee on notice of an enforcement event without the provider's consent and without informing it in advance, and allows the pledgee to demand payment directly from the debtor of a pledged monetary claim. Article 11(2) sets out the public-auction machinery in detail, with a Luxembourg bailiff or notary as auctioneer, at least eight working days' press notice with prescribed content, sale to the highest bidder with payment permitted by set-off against the secured obligations, and minutes within three working days. The enforcement event is whatever the parties agree under Article 1(6). Lender-side, choose and specify the route and the valuation method in the security agreement, because Article 11 is a menu and the opening words "unless otherwise provided for" mean the drafting can narrow it as well as widen it.
jurisdiction.financial_collateral_regime: The instrument is the Law of 5 August 2005 on financial collateral arrangements, transposing Directive 2002/47/EC and repealing the earlier repurchase and transfer-of-ownership-for-security laws. On the scope of persons, natural-person collateral providers ARE covered, in contrast to England: the Law contains no requirement that both parties be non-natural persons, Article 2(1) expressly contemplates financial collateral arrangements and netting agreements entered into either by a merchant or a non-merchant, and Article 20(4) carves the Law of 8 December 2000 on over-indebtedness out of the general disapplication of insolvency law, a carve-out that only makes sense if private individuals are within scope. [VERIFY] that last step is an inference from the primary text rather than an express scope provision, the Law having no scope article naming eligible persons, and it must be confirmed by Luxembourg counsel before it leaves draft. The core benefits sit in Articles 20 and 21: financial collateral arrangements, the agreed enforcement events, netting agreements and the agreed valuation and enforcement measures are valid and enforceable against third parties, commissioners, receivers and liquidators notwithstanding reorganisation measures, winding-up proceedings or any other similar national or foreign proceedings under Article 20(1); termination, valuation, enforcement and netting triggered by an enforcement procedure or protective measure are deemed to have occurred before it under Article 20(2); the listed civil, commercial and national or foreign insolvency, attachment and similar provisions do not apply, with the over-indebtedness law the sole carve-out under Article 20(4); the same rules apply on the death or incapacity of the collateral provider or the debtor under the final paragraph of Article 20(4); arrangements made on the day of opening but before the court decision are valid, and arrangements made after it are valid if the taker proves it neither knew nor should have known, under Article 21. Article 24 confirms that the disapplied national provisions remain disapplied where the collateral provider is established or resident in Luxembourg.
jurisdiction.governing_law_of_intermediated_securitie: Article 23 is Luxembourg's PRIMA rule and it mirrors the English account-location rule almost exactly: any question on the listed matters arising in relation to financial collateral over financial instruments transferable by book entry is governed by the law of the country in which the relevant account is maintained, meaning its domestic law with renvoi excluded. The matters covered are the legal nature and proprietary effects, the requirements for provision and for third-party effectiveness, extinction or subordination by a competing interest or a good-faith acquisition, the custodian's obligations to a competing claimant, the conditions for realisation after an enforcement event, and the extent of the arrangement over dividends, income, distributions, reimbursements and proceeds. Relevant account is defined in Article 1(3) as the register or account in which the entries providing the collateral are made, which may be maintained by the collateral taker itself. Luxembourg is not a contracting party to the 2006 Hague Securities Convention, so there is no choice-of-law route to displace the account-location rule. The practical consequence is the same as England's: the account booking location, not the governing law of the pledge agreement, drives the proprietary analysis.
jurisdiction.practical_notes: (1) If the bank is the Luxembourg custodian, Article 5(2)(a)(i) means the pledge agreement alone perfects, which is the cheapest structure of the three jurisdictions; if a third-party custodian holds, use the Article 5(2)(a)(ii) route and take the custodian's acknowledgement in writing, remembering that this route is treated as the custodian waiving its own ranking unless it says otherwise. (2) Use the Article 4 all-present-and-future formulation so that substitutions in a revolving portfolio do not need new security, and rely on Article 2(3) so that the client's right to trade the portfolio until a default notice does not undermine the pledge, which is a genuine structural advantage over English law. (3) Specify the valuation method in the security agreement, because Article 11(1)(a) appropriation is priced by the agreed valuation method, and without one the lender is pushed toward private sale in a commercially reasonable manner or auction. (4) Enforcement without prior notice is the statutory default, but Article 11(1) opens with "unless otherwise provided for", so do not let a negotiated notice period creep into the security agreement unless it is meant, and if the client insists put it in the facility letter as a courtesy undertaking rather than as a condition of the enforcement power. (5) For a natural-person pledgor the Law applies, but the over-indebtedness carve-out in Article 20(4) means full insolvency remoteness cannot be assumed against a Luxembourg-resident individual, so have Luxembourg counsel scope the over-indebtedness procedure for the specific client. (6) For a third-party pledgor the Law is comfortable with security for a third party's obligations and with fiduciary or agent structures under Article 2(4), and Article 2(6) even allows the provider to waive its recourse claims against the principal debtor, valid against third parties, but corporate benefit and, for an individual, independent advice remain ordinary diligence items. (7) The death or incapacity rule in Article 20(4) is directly useful for a private-client pledgor and is worth citing in the events-of-default rationale.

clauses.title: Facility type: uncommitted and repayable on demand versus committed term
clauses.opening_text: The facility is uncommitted. The Bank is not obliged to make any advance, and each utilisation is a separate decision of the Bank whether or not the conditions precedent are satisfied and whether or not the Limit is undrawn. The facility has no fixed term. The Bank may at any time, in its discretion and without giving a reason, reduce, suspend or cancel the Limit and may demand immediate repayment of all principal, interest, fees and other amounts outstanding, whether or not any Event of Default has occurred and whether or not the Borrower is in compliance with the margin requirement. A demand is effective when made, and the Bank is not required to give any notice beyond the demand itself. No failure or delay by the Bank in demanding repayment or in cancelling the Limit operates as a waiver of the right to do so, and no course of dealing converts the facility into a committed one.
clauses.opening_rationale: The demand right is what the Bank has instead of covenants, and it is the reason this product can be priced and sized the way it is. If the Bank has to prove an event of default before it can stop, it is arguing about materiality while the collateral is moving, and the argument costs more than the margin it was protecting. Every published private-bank document opened for this playbook takes this position, so it is the market opening rather than an aggressive one. What the Borrower buys with it is price, size and speed of execution, which is the whole appeal of borrowing against a portfolio instead of against a covenant package.

ladder.text: The facility is uncommitted and all amounts outstanding are repayable on demand. Where the Bank cancels or reduces the Limit for convenience, meaning otherwise than in the circumstances described below, it will give the Borrower not less than X days' prior notice, during which the Borrower may not draw further amounts. That notice period does not apply, and the Bank may cancel, reduce or demand with immediate effect, where: an Event of Default has occurred; a margin shortfall is outstanding and uncured; the collateral has ceased to satisfy the eligible collateral or concentration requirements; the cancellation, reduction or demand is required by or results from any law, regulation or requirement of a regulator, exchange or clearing system; or the Bank determines that the circumstances on which the Limit was granted have materially changed. Nothing in this clause obliges the Bank to make any advance at any time.
ladder.rationale: This concession is a queue, not a brake. The Bank almost never leaves a Lombard line for convenience: it leaves because something has happened, and everything that actually happens is carved out, so the notice period bites only in the case where the Bank was in no hurry anyway. It is also the published position of a real Luxembourg template, which makes it an easy thing to say yes to and a useful thing to have said yes to when the harder clauses come up. The sentence to use in the room is that the Bank will not walk away from a client without warning, but it will not stand still while the portfolio falls.

ladder.text: The Bank commits to make advances up to the Limit until the date falling X months after the date of the facility letter, subject to the conditions precedent being satisfied on each funding date and to the lending value of the collateral, immediately after the advance, being not less than the amount then outstanding. The Bank may cancel any undrawn commitment and declare all amounts outstanding immediately due and payable on any of the following: a margin shortfall that is not cured within the cure period; any Event of Default; the insolvency, or the death or incapacity, of the Borrower or of any Pledgor; the illegality of, or any regulatory requirement affecting, the Bank's performance; any material misrepresentation; any breach of the eligible collateral or concentration requirements; the insolvency of, delisting of, or a suspension of trading of more than X trading days in, any pledged security; a change of control of the Borrower; or a fall in the price of any pledged security below the level stated in the facility letter. The Bank is not obliged to advance while a margin call is outstanding or while any of the above is continuing, and the commitment does not renew or roll over except by a further decision of the Bank. Prepayment is subject to the breakage provisions of the facility letter.
ladder.rationale: Term can be conceded, but only by buying the demand right back in pieces, and the list has to reach both of the things the demand right reaches automatically: the collateral getting worse and the Borrower getting worse. If it does, the Bank has traded flexibility for documentation rather than for risk. The honest line to the counterparty is that a term facility is available and that everything the demand right was doing silently will now be written down, and the written version is usually less comfortable to read than the demand right it replaces. Because this tier changes the product rather than a term of it, the default floor for this clause is set at acceptable: moving to committed term should always be an escalation and never a deal lawyer's decision.
conditions: Collateral is exchange-listed or daily-dealt and within the concentration limit at signing and on each funding date.
The Bank or a member of its group is the Custodian, or an executed account control agreement is in place.
Credit has priced the commitment, including breakage and the cost of the undrawn line.
Where the Borrower is an individual, any declaration and statement on which the facility's regulatory treatment depends is in place before signing.
The mandatory prepayment list has been read against the events of default clause so that nothing is lost in the gap between them.
The lending values applied have been reduced to reflect that the Bank cannot exit the commitment at will.

ladder.text: The Bank will not agree a committed facility with no collateral-linked mandatory prepayment right; will not commit to advance on a funding date irrespective of the lending value of the collateral on that date; will not accept a demand right exercisable only after an Event of Default or only after a cure period has run; will not agree an evergreen or automatically renewing commitment that the Bank cannot decline to renew; will not agree that it may not demand repayment or cancel the Limit while the Borrower is within the margin requirement; and will not accept a notice period for cancellation that continues to run where an Event of Default, an uncured margin shortfall, an illegality or a regulatory requirement has occurred.
ladder.rationale: Each of these turns a secured, exit-at-will facility into an unsecured-style commitment that happens to have a portfolio attached to it. The whole premise of the product is that the Bank's exposure is to assets it can value daily and leave quickly; a commitment that survives those assets deteriorating is a commitment to lend against something else entirely. The funding-date point is not theoretical either: the commentary in the source pool records that collateral moves between signing and funding, so a facility committed on day one can already be in margin call by the time it is drawn, and the Bank would be funding into a shortfall it is contractually barred from refusing.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: The published Luxembourg template is the closest thing in the source pool to the acceptable tier written out: an authorisation to run a debit balance up to a Limit, granted at the bank's sole discretion for an indefinite period, with either party able to terminate on 90 days' notice and the bank able to terminate with immediate effect on any listed event of default (BANK-LU-01). The same document also records a 14 calendar day withdrawal right for a retail client on a distance contract where the facility is unused, which is a consumer-protection feature of the booking centre rather than a negotiated term and should be checked with the booking centre before the facility letter is issued.
escalation_triggers: Any request to convert the facility from uncommitted demand to committed term.
Any request for a notice period longer than X days before the Bank may cancel or reduce the Limit.
Any request that a notice period apply where an Event of Default, an uncured margin shortfall, an illegality or a regulatory requirement has occurred.
Any request that the demand right be exercisable only on an Event of Default, or be subject to a cure period.
Any request for automatic renewal, rollover or an evergreen commitment.
Any request that the Bank commit to advance without re-testing the lending value on the funding date.
not_automated: Whether to exercise the demand right on a live facility, as against forbearing while the relationship is discussed. The clause fixes who decides; it does not decide.
Whether to offer committed term at all for relationship reasons, and what that costs in lending value, price and commitment fee.
Whether repeated forbearance has made an uncommitted line committed in substance. That is a course-of-dealing judgement, and no rule in this library can make it.
Setting the notice period and the term length. Only one opened source states either figure, and both are the institution's risk appetite.

clauses.title: Conditions precedent to first and each utilisation
clauses.opening_text: The Bank is not obliged to make the first advance until it has received, in form and substance satisfactory to it, each of the following: (a) identification, know-your-client, sanctions screening and source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence for the Borrower, each Pledgor and each beneficial owner, controller, settlor, protector and authorised signatory of either; (b) the constitutional, trust or partnership documents establishing that the Borrower and each Pledgor exists, and the resolutions, consents and authorities establishing that it has power to enter into the finance documents and to grant the security and that the signatories are authorised; (c) the facility letter, the security agreement and, where the Custodian is not the Bank or a member of its group, the account control agreement, each executed; (d) evidence that every step required to make the security effective and to give the Bank possession or control under the law governing the security has been completed, including the opening of the pledged accounts and the booking, earmarking or notification required by that law; (e) a confirmation from the Custodian of the holdings in the pledged accounts and of the waiver or subordination of the Custodian's own liens, rights of retention and rights of set-off over those accounts; (f) a legal opinion satisfactory to the Bank where any obligor, pledgor or asset is outside the jurisdiction whose law governs the security; (g) evidence satisfactory to the Bank that the pledged assets are eligible collateral, are free of transfer restrictions other than those disclosed, and settle through the ordinary book-entry system; (h) each compliance, tax and regulatory sign-off that the Bank requires in connection with the facility, the Borrower, any Pledgor or the pledged assets; and (i) such other documents, evidence, authorisations and assurances as the Bank may require. Each condition in this clause must also be satisfied on the date of, and immediately after, each further utilisation, and by accepting the proceeds of any advance the Borrower is deemed to repeat, on that date, the representations to which those conditions relate. Nothing in this clause obliges the Bank to make any advance, whether or not every condition has been satisfied.
clauses.opening_rationale: Conditions precedent are the only point in the life of a facility where the Bank has complete leverage, because nothing has left the building yet, and everything on this list is materially harder to obtain the day after drawdown than the day before. The list is also where the whole library plugs in: capacity, insider status, perfection and the regulatory perimeter are all cleared here rather than being blocked at the term sheet, which is why the playbook rules add to this clause rather than stopping the deal. Re-testing on each utilisation is not belt-and-braces on an uncommitted facility; it is what stops a clean day-one file being used to draw into a portfolio that has since changed. Saying yes to the list costs the Borrower a week of administration; saying no to it costs the Bank its security.

ladder.text: The Bank is not obliged to make the first advance until it has received each of the documents and items listed in the conditions precedent schedule, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to it, together with such other documents, evidence, authorisations and assurances as the Bank may reasonably require. The Bank will confirm to the Borrower within X business days of receipt of the last outstanding item that the conditions precedent have been satisfied. Where the condition relates to the eligibility of the pledged assets or to the absence of transfer restrictions, it is satisfied where the Bank is reasonably satisfied. The conditions must also be satisfied on the date of, and immediately after, each further utilisation, and by accepting the proceeds of any advance the Borrower is deemed to repeat, on that date, the representations to which those conditions relate. Nothing in this clause obliges the Bank to make any advance.
ladder.rationale: A reasonableness qualifier on the Bank's satisfaction changes the standard, not the list, and the standard was never the protection: the protection is that the money does not move until the file is complete. It is also the observed outcome in a filed institutional margin loan, so the Bank is conceding to the market rather than below it, and it removes the counterparty's best argument, which is that the Bank could refuse to fund by simply declaring itself unsatisfied with a document that is plainly fine. Committing to confirm satisfaction within a short window costs nothing and buys the Borrower the thing it actually wants here, which is certainty of timing for a purchase or a repayment it has already scheduled.
conditions: The sweeper survives in qualified form; it is not deleted.
Reasonableness attaches to the Bank's satisfaction, not to the question whether an item is required at all.

ladder.text: The conditions precedent are those set out in the conditions precedent schedule, together with any condition the Bank notifies to the Borrower before the facility letter is signed. The Bank may make the first advance before it has received the items identified in Part 2 of that schedule, being documents of an administrative character which do not affect the existence, validity, priority or enforceability of the security, against the Borrower's undertaking to deliver them within X business days of the date of first utilisation; failure to deliver within that period is an Event of Default. The Bank will not make any advance until it has received each item in Part 1 of that schedule, being: identification, know-your-client, sanctions and source-of-funds evidence; the documents evidencing the capacity and authority of the Borrower and each Pledgor and the authority of the signatories; the executed finance documents and security documents; every step required to make the security effective and to give the Bank possession or control under the law governing it, including an executed account control agreement where the Custodian is not the Bank or a member of its group; every compliance sign-off that the Bank requires; and any declaration, statement or other document which, under any law or regulation applicable to the facility, must be made or delivered before the facility letter is entered into. A condition may be waived only by the Bank in writing, a waiver is effective only for the utilisation to which it relates, and no waiver or delay affects the Bank's right to require the condition on any later utilisation.
ladder.rationale: This tier gives the Borrower what it is actually asking for, which is to know at signing what it has to produce and by when, and it gives it up in the only place where it is safe to give up: documents that are awkward to chase but that do not decide whether the Bank has security. The line between Part 1 and Part 2 is the whole clause, and it is not drawn by convenience but by a test anyone can apply in the room, which is whether the item can still be fixed the day after the money moves. Perfection cannot, because the priority date has gone. A pre-agreement regulatory declaration cannot, because the sequence is what the exemption depends on. Insider clearance cannot, because by then the Bank has taken the pledge. The undertaking plus an event of default is the enforcement mechanism for everything else, and it is enough for a file of certificates.
conditions: Part 2 contains no item that affects the existence, validity, priority or enforceability of the security.
Part 2 contains no item required by law or regulation to exist before the facility letter is entered into.
Part 2 contains no compliance, sanctions or source-of-funds item.
The Bank or a member of its group is the Custodian, or the account control agreement is already executed.
The Borrower is not an individual to whom a consumer or regulated-credit regime may apply, or the position has been cleared by compliance.

ladder.text: The Bank will not accept know-your-client, sanctions, source-of-funds, capacity or authority evidence, security perfection steps (including an account control agreement where a third party is the Custodian), or a compliance sign-off, being given as a post-closing undertaking or a representation instead of as a condition to advance; will not accept a condition being deemed satisfied by the passage of time or by the Bank's failure to respond; will not accept the deletion of the sweeper, so that the Bank is confined at signing to a list it has to complete before it has seen the structure; will not accept an opinion addressed to the Borrower rather than to the Bank, or a director's certificate in place of an opinion, where an opinion is required; will not accept a declaration or statement on which the regulatory treatment of the facility depends being made after the facility letter is entered into; and will not accept a term that requires the Bank to advance once the conditions are satisfied.
ladder.rationale: Each of these moves an item from the one moment when it can be obtained to a moment when it cannot. A post-closing perfection undertaking is worth exactly what the Borrower is worth on the day the security turns out to be defective, which is the same day the Bank needed the security. Deemed satisfaction is worse than it sounds, because the Bank's silence usually means the file is being reviewed, not that it is clean. And a declaration signed after the agreement does not make an exempt agreement exempt: the statute requires it before, so the sequence is the whole protection and it cannot be regularised afterwards. On an uncommitted facility the final limb matters too, because an obligation to advance once conditions are met would quietly convert the facility into a committed one.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: The conditions precedent should name which of the statutory possession routes the deal is using, because they are alternatives and the security agreement has to match the one chosen. For book-entry financial instruments the routes are: concluding the pledge agreement where the pledgee is itself the custodian; a three-party agreement with the custodian, or a two-party agreement notified to it, under which the custodian will act on the pledgee's instructions without any further agreement of the provider; booking the instruments to an account of the pledgee; or earmarking them in the custodian's books (LAW-LU-01, art. 5(2)(a)). Where the deal uses any route other than the first, the custodian is treated as having waived its own pledge ranking unless otherwise agreed or notified, so the CP should capture that in writing. A right of substitution, a right to withdraw excess collateral, a right to collect proceeds and a reserved right of the provider to give instructions do not prejudice the collateral having been provided (LAW-LU-01, art. 2(3)), which is a materially easier position than the English one and means the CP list does not have to strip the client's ordinary account rights. [VERIFY] The WP7 research file additionally records that instruments evidencing a financial collateral arrangement are not subject to registration formalities under art. 26 of the same law; that article was not among those read by the sourcing agent or by this drafting agent.
cps: [R12_third_party_custodian] Account control agreement executed by the third-party custodian, acknowledging the lender's security, agreeing to act on the lender's instructions without further consent from the account holder, and subordinating or waiving the custodian's own liens and rights of set-off over the account.

clauses.title: Eligible collateral and lending values by asset class
clauses.opening_text: Eligible collateral is limited to the asset classes listed in the Eligible Collateral Schedule to this facility letter. The lending value of a pledged asset is the market value of that asset as determined by the Bank multiplied by the lending value percentage the Bank applies to the relevant asset class from time to time, and the Bank may apply a different percentage to an individual holding. An asset that is not listed in the Eligible Collateral Schedule has a lending value of nil, and each of the following has a lending value of nil whether or not its asset class is listed: any security subject to a transfer restriction, lock-up, escrow arrangement or issuer consent requirement; any unlisted security or other asset for which the Bank does not have a pricing source it considers reliable; any interest in a fund whose redemptions are suspended, gated, deferred or side-pocketed; and any security suspended from trading or subject to a market-wide or issuer-specific trading restriction. Where a pledged asset is denominated in a currency other than the currency of the facility, its lending value is reduced by a further X percentage points to reflect currency risk. The Bank may amend the Eligible Collateral Schedule and any lending value percentage in accordance with the lender discretion clause of this facility letter.
clauses.opening_rationale: This is the clause that decides how much money leaves the building against a given portfolio, so the Bank keeps both halves of the calculation: what counts as collateral, and at what rate. Every published bank document opened for this playbook states the lending value as a bank-set percentage of a bank-determined value and reserves the right to change it. The exclusions are not decoration: an asset the Bank cannot price, or cannot sell on the day it needs to sell, has no lending value whatever its screen price, and the Swiss regulator's stated concern about Lombard books is that haircuts are set too low, not too high. The currency haircut is there because an exchange-rate move can exhaust the cover without the securities moving at all.

ladder.text: Eligible collateral is limited to the asset classes listed in the Eligible Collateral Schedule. The Bank calculates the lending value of each pledged asset acting in good faith, as the market value of that asset multiplied by the lending value percentage applying to the relevant asset class, using prices taken from the pricing sources identified in the Schedule or, where no such price is available, a price determined by the Bank acting in good faith. The Bank reviews lending value percentages at intervals of not less than X and, on request, tells the Borrower the percentages then applying; the Bank notifies the Borrower of a change as soon as reasonably practicable after it takes effect. Assets excluded under the preferred position remain of nil lending value, and the currency haircut applies in accordance with the haircut matrix set out in the Schedule.
ladder.rationale: Conceding good faith and a named pricing source costs the Bank nothing it wants to keep. It is already how the calculation is done operationally, and a published retail Lombard template in the source pool concedes exactly this. What the Bank keeps is the percentage itself and the exclusions, which is where the credit protection sits. Publishing the haircut matrix also gives the relationship manager something to point at instead of an argument, which is worth more than the flexibility it gives up.

ladder.text: The lending value percentages applying to the holdings identified in Part 1 of the Eligible Collateral Schedule are fixed for X months from the date of this facility letter, and within that period the Bank may change them only on X business days' prior written notice, except where the change is required by law or regulation, where the asset has ceased to be eligible under the exclusions in this clause, or where the Bank determines that the market value of the relevant asset class is declining rapidly, in each of which cases the change takes effect immediately. Where a pledged asset is not exchange-listed and is valued by reference to a net asset value or other value reported by or on behalf of the issuer, the Borrower may, once in any X month period and at its own cost, require the Bank to obtain a valuation from an independent valuer appointed by the Bank; the Bank will take that valuation into account, and the Bank's determination following it is final. All other lending value percentages, and the Eligible Collateral Schedule itself, remain amendable by the Bank at any time.
ladder.rationale: This is the furthest the Bank should go, and because it is a real concession it is fenced. Fixing a percentage for a named holding for a stated period turns a risk-management tool into a commercial term, which is only tolerable where the collateral is liquid, diversified and priced by the market rather than by the issuer. The carve-outs are the price of the concession: a fixed percentage cannot survive a change in law, an asset becoming ineligible, or a rapid decline, because those are the moments the percentage exists for. The appraisal right is capped at one valuation a period, at the Borrower's cost, with the Bank appointing the valuer and keeping the final determination, so it informs the decision without transferring it.
conditions: Collateral is limited to exchange-listed securities, daily-dealt funds and cash.
No holding in Part 1 of the Schedule is a restricted, locked-up or control security.
Single-name exposure is within the concentration limit set for the facility.
The Bank or a member of its group is the Custodian, or an executed account control agreement is in place.
Credit has priced both the fixed percentages and the length of the fixing period.

ladder.text: The Bank will not agree a lending-value grid fixed for the life of the facility or amendable only with the Borrower's consent; will not give a positive lending value to unlisted securities, gated or suspended fund interests, restricted or locked-up stock, or any asset it cannot price from a source it has chosen; will not accept a valuation supplied by the Borrower, by the issuer, or by a valuer appointed by the Borrower as binding on it; will not remove the currency haircut where the facility currency and a collateral currency differ; and will not accept a term under which an asset stays eligible after it has become subject to a transfer restriction or a trading suspension.
ladder.rationale: Each of these moves the lending value from being the Bank's own measure of risk to being something the Borrower or a third party controls, and once that happens the clause has no purpose left. The exclusions in particular are the difference between a secured facility and an unsecured one: an asset that cannot be sold inside the cure period is not collateral. Conceding a borrower-supplied valuation would also leave the Bank arguing about price at exactly the moment it needs to sell, which is the position every enforcement provision in this playbook is written to avoid.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: Draw the eligibility schedule against the statutory exit routes: listed instruments can be appropriated at market price, and fund units at the last published net asset value provided it is less than a year old, or at the fund's redemption price (LAW-LU-01, art. 11(1)(e)-(f)). Collateral that cannot be priced by one of those routes has no fast exit under Luxembourg law, which is a direct argument for giving it a nil lending value rather than a low one.

Any request to admit unlisted, gated, suspended, restricted or locked-up assets to the Eligible Collateral Schedule at a positive lending value.
Any request for a valuation supplied or appointed by the Borrower to bind the Bank.
Any bespoke lending value percentage above the Bank's standard percentage for that asset class.
Any request to remove the currency haircut where the facility currency and a collateral currency differ.

Setting the numeric grid itself. The demonstrator carries X placeholders because no public source opened for this playbook publishes one.
Whether an asset that becomes illiquid or restricted after drawdown is re-rated immediately or on notice.

clauses.title: Concentration limits by issuer, asset class and currency
clauses.opening_text: Collateral is eligible only to the extent it is diversified in accordance with this clause. So much of the lending value attributable to securities of any one issuer as exceeds X per cent. of the total lending value of the collateral is disregarded, and so much as is attributable to issuers within the same group, the same industry sector or the same currency as exceeds X per cent. of the total lending value is likewise disregarded. The Bank determines whether issuers form a group, sector or correlated set. Neither the Borrower nor any of its affiliates or connected persons will grant security over, or agree to pledge, securities of the same class as any pledged security to any other financier without the Bank's consent. If the Bank considers that the collateral is not sufficiently diversified it may, at its option and without prejudice to its other rights, reduce the lending value of the affected securities, require the Borrower to post further eligible collateral or repay, charge a differentiated fee, or treat the position as an event entitling the Bank to realise the collateral in accordance with this facility letter.
clauses.opening_rationale: Concentration is the risk this product actually fails on: the Bank can be perfectly secured on paper and still not get out, because selling a large stake in one name moves the price against it. That is why the clause bites on lending value rather than market value, and why correlated names are grouped rather than counted separately. The Swiss regulator names single-stock lending and undiversified collateral as a supervisory focus, so the Bank is not inventing a concern here. The same-class negative pledge matters as much as the cap: several margin loans stacked on one stock create an overhang that turns three lenders' exits into one queue.

ladder.text: The single-name limit is X per cent. of the total lending value of the collateral and is set out in the Eligible Collateral Schedule. Lending value attributable to an issuer above that limit is taken at a reduced lending value percentage determined by the Bank rather than disregarded entirely, and the Bank will tell the Borrower the limit and the reduced percentage then applying on request. The Bank may change the limit in accordance with the lender discretion clause of this facility letter. A breach of the limit is not of itself an event of default, but requires the Borrower to post further eligible collateral, repay or substitute collateral within the cure period in the margin maintenance clause, and while a breach continues the Bank need not make further advances.
ladder.rationale: Taking the excess at a reduced lending value rather than at nil gives the Borrower a portfolio that behaves sensibly as prices move, and it keeps the Bank's protection intact because the reduction is still the Bank's number. Routing a breach through the margin mechanics rather than straight to default is also the right sequencing: a concentration breach usually arises from a price move, not misconduct, and the Bank's remedy is more collateral, not enforcement. Stopping further advances while the breach continues is what keeps the position from being made worse while it is being cured.

ladder.text: The single-name limit is X per cent. of the total lending value of the collateral and the Bank will not reduce it for X months from the date of this facility letter except on X business days' prior written notice, and may reduce it with immediate effect only where the change is required by law or regulation, where the relevant security ceases to be eligible, or where the Bank determines that the market value or traded liquidity of the relevant security is declining rapidly. The holdings identified in Part 2 of the Eligible Collateral Schedule are treated as within the limit at the date of this facility letter notwithstanding that they exceed it, provided that the Borrower does not increase them and that the excess is taken at the reduced lending value percentage stated in the Schedule. The same-class undertaking applies to the Borrower and to any entity it controls, rather than to all of its affiliates and connected persons. Insufficient diversification is a repricing and collateral top-up event and is not of itself a ground for realisation.
ladder.rationale: Every element of this is a genuine loss of protection, which is why it needs credit approval and conditions rather than a deal lawyer's signature. Grandfathering a concentrated holding is defensible only if it cannot grow and only if it is already carried at a lending value that assumes a difficult exit. Narrowing the same-class undertaking to controlled entities is the concession most often asked for and the least damaging, because it still stops the Borrower stacking financings on the same stock through vehicles it directs. Giving up the stand-alone realisation right is survivable only because the margin mechanics still deliver an enforcement route once the position is not cured.
conditions: The grandfathered holding is exchange-listed, liquid and not restricted, locked-up or control stock.
The excess is carried at a reduced lending value percentage priced by credit.
The Borrower undertakes not to increase the grandfathered holding.
Neither the Borrower nor the Pledgor is a PDMR or insider of the concentrated issuer.
The margin maintenance cure period for this facility is at or tighter than its default floor.

ladder.text: The Bank will not lend against a concentrated portfolio with no concentration discipline at all, meaning no single-name limit, no reduction in lending value for the concentrated position and no same-class undertaking. It will not agree that concentration is tested against market value rather than lending value, that a limit once set can never be changed, or that a breach discovered after drawdown has no consequence until maturity. It will not accept a term preventing it from treating issuers in the same group, sector or currency as a single exposure, or from re-testing concentration during the life of the facility.
ladder.rationale: A single-stock facility can be a perfectly good transaction, but only when it is priced as one: the lender's answer to concentration is a lower lending value and a negative pledge, not indifference. If the Bank can neither cap the exposure, nor discount it, nor stop the same stock being pledged elsewhere, it has written an unsecured loan with extra paperwork. Testing against market value rather than lending value would also hide exactly the exposure the clause exists to measure, because the concentrated name is usually the one carrying the largest haircut.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: A published Luxembourg bank template treats insufficient diversification as an input to the limit, as a ground for differentiated fees, and as a stand-alone ground for unilateral realisation without prior notice (BANK-LU-01), which is consistent with enforcement without prior notice being the statutory default under the financial collateral law unless the parties provide otherwise (LAW-LU-01, art. 11). The practical point for drafting is that the stand-alone diversification trigger is worth more in Luxembourg than elsewhere, so give it up knowingly rather than as a tidy-up.

Any request to grandfather an existing holding above the single-name limit.
Any request to remove or narrow the same-class negative pledge beyond entities the Borrower controls.
Any request to fix the single-name limit for the life of the facility or to require the Borrower's consent to change it.
Any request to test concentration against market value rather than lending value.

Whether two issuers are correlated enough to be treated as one exposure.
Whether to grandfather an existing concentrated holding, and at what reduced lending value.

clauses.title: Lender discretion over valuation, lending values and eligibility
clauses.opening_text: The Bank may at any time, in its discretion and with immediate effect, determine and re-determine the market value of any pledged asset, change the lending value percentage applying to any asset class or to any individual holding, add an asset class to or remove one from the Eligible Collateral Schedule, and determine that a pledged asset has ceased to be eligible. The Bank values the collateral at least daily using pricing sources it selects. A change takes effect when the Bank makes it, whether or not the Bank has notified the Borrower and whether or not a margin call is then outstanding; the Bank will inform the Borrower of the change by any means it considers appropriate. No change requires the consent of the Borrower or of the Pledgor.
clauses.opening_rationale: The ability to reprice risk the same day is the core protection behind an uncommitted facility, and it is what the Bank has instead of covenants. If the Bank has to wait, it is holding a fixed-rate view of a moving portfolio, and the loss it takes in the waiting period is exactly the loss the haircut was set to avoid. Every published bank document opened for this playbook takes this position, so it is the market opening rather than an aggressive one. It is also honest about what the facility is: the Borrower is buying liquidity against a portfolio, not buying a fixed advance rate for a term.

ladder.text: The Bank may at any time determine and re-determine the market value of any pledged asset, change the lending value percentage applying to any asset class or holding, and change the composition of the Eligible Collateral Schedule, in each case acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner and with immediate effect. The Bank will notify the Borrower of a change as soon as reasonably practicable after it takes effect, and will on request provide the calculation and the principal parameters used to determine a lending value or a collateral shortfall. No change requires the consent of the Borrower or of the Pledgor.
ladder.rationale: This is a standard, not a delay, and that distinction is the whole of the concession. A good-faith and commercially reasonable standard binds the Bank to a process it already follows, and the English authority on appropriation confirms that what has to be reasonable is the manner of valuation judged objectively, not the result, so the Bank is not underwriting the outcome. Agreeing to show the calculation is also good defensive practice: under Swiss law a bank that cannot produce the parameters behind a call exposes itself to liability, so the Bank should be able to do this anyway. The Bank gives up the word "absolute" and keeps the timing, which is the part that has economic value.

ladder.text: Where the Bank changes the lending value percentage applying to an asset class or removes an asset class from the Eligible Collateral Schedule, the change takes effect X business days after the Bank has notified the Borrower. That notice period does not apply, and the change takes effect immediately, where: the change is required by or results from any law, regulation, or requirement of a regulator, exchange or clearing system; the Bank determines that the market value or the traded liquidity of the relevant asset class or holding is declining rapidly or that a market disruption has occurred; the relevant asset has ceased to be eligible under the eligible collateral clause, including because it has become subject to a transfer restriction, a trading suspension or a redemption gate; or a margin call is outstanding and uncured. The Bank may in all cases determine and re-determine market value at any time and with immediate effect, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner, and nothing in this clause requires the Bank to make an advance.
ladder.rationale: The notice period is the single most-asked-for concession on this clause, and it is conceded here in the only shape that survives contact with a falling market: a period for routine repricing, and immediate effect for the four situations in which a period would cause the loss it is meant to prevent. Put plainly to the counterparty, the Bank is saying it will not change the rules on you in a quiet market without warning, but it will not stand still in a loud one. The carve-out for an open margin call matters more than it looks: without it the Borrower could hold the Bank to a stale lending value for the length of the notice period precisely when the collateral is deteriorating. Note also that the Bank keeps the right to re-mark value at any time even in this tier, because valuation and lending value are different levers and only one of them is being slowed down.
conditions: Collateral is diversified within the concentration limit and is exchange-listed or daily-dealt.
The facility is the Bank's only exposure to the Borrower, or other exposures have been considered by credit.
The Bank or a member of its group is the Custodian, or an executed account control agreement is in place.
The margin maintenance cure period is at or tighter than its default floor for this deal.
Credit has confirmed the notice period is priced into the lending values applied.

ladder.text: The Bank will not make a change to lending values, haircuts or eligibility conditional on the Borrower's or the Pledgor's consent; will not accept a notice period that applies where the change is required by law or regulation, where collateral value or liquidity is falling rapidly, where the asset has ceased to be eligible, or while a margin call is outstanding; will not agree that it may revalue or reprice only on the occurrence of a defined external event or only at fixed intervals; will not agree to suspend revaluation, or to freeze lending values, while a call or a dispute is open; and will not accept a third-party determination of value that binds the Bank or that suspends a change until the determination is made.
ladder.rationale: Each of these converts the Bank's risk lever into something the Borrower or a third party can hold down, and always at the worst moment, because the only time a borrower wants to freeze the lending value is when it is about to fall. A notice period that runs through a rapid decline is not a notice period, it is an unfunded put written by the Bank. Objective-trigger-only drafting fails for the same reason: the events that damage a Lombard book are usually visible in liquidity and price behaviour well before anything anyone has defined as a market event has occurred.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: The Bank's valuation discretion is bounded at the exit by the statutory pricing routes: on appropriation, listed instruments are taken at market price and fund units at the last published net asset value provided it is less than a year old, or at the fund's redemption price (LAW-LU-01, art. 11(1)(e)-(f)). [VERIFY] Luxembourg practice is also said to be to specify the agreed valuation method in the security agreement, because appropriation under art. 11(1)(a) is priced by that agreed method; that point comes from the WP7 research file (docs/research/jurisdictions_research.md) and was not confirmed against the primary text by this agent. Note separately that a published Luxembourg template is the high-water mark of lender discretion in the whole source pool (BANK-LU-01), so a Luxembourg counterparty is unlikely to be able to say the preferred position is off-market.
escalation_triggers: Any request for a notice period longer than X business days before a change in lending values takes effect.
Any request to remove or narrow one of the four immediate-effect carve-outs, and in particular the rapid-decline or open-margin-call carve-out.
Any request that the Bank may not change lending values while a margin call is outstanding.
Any request for a binding third-party valuation, or for a dispute mechanism that suspends a change pending determination.
Any request to limit revaluation to fixed intervals or to defined external market events.
Any request that a change requires the Borrower's or the Pledgor's consent.
not_automated: Whether a particular market move is a "rapid decline" that collapses the notice period. The clause defines who decides, not what the answer is.
Whether to exercise the discretion at all on a live position, as against forbearing while the relationship is discussed.
Setting the notice period itself. Only one opened source concedes one (15 days) and the number here is the institution's risk appetite.
Whether to disclose the full haircut matrix to a counterparty who asks for it during negotiation.

clauses.title: Margin maintenance, margin call mechanics and cure period
clauses.opening_text: A Collateral Shortfall arises whenever the Lending Value of the pledged assets is less than X per cent of the aggregate of all amounts outstanding and all contingent and unmatured liabilities of the Borrower to the Bank (the Trigger Level), as determined by the Bank at any time. On a Collateral Shortfall the Borrower must immediately, on demand and without any prior notice being required, either repay, or pledge further Eligible Collateral acceptable to the Bank, or a combination of the two, in an amount sufficient to restore the Lending Value to Y per cent of those amounts (the Restoration Level), calculated on the values determined by the Bank on the day the demand is made. The Bank may notify the Borrower of a Collateral Shortfall and may allow a period within which it is to be met, but is obliged to do neither; any period the Bank allows is revocable by the Bank at any time, does not arise again on a subsequent Collateral Shortfall, and is not a condition precedent to, and does not suspend, any right of the Bank under the enforcement clause. A second Collateral Shortfall arising while an earlier one is uncured does not extend any period then running.
clauses.opening_rationale: The Bank is lending against a price it does not control, so the only protection it has is the speed with which it can turn a fall in that price back into cash. The two-level structure is what makes that work: a call that only restores the position to the Trigger Level puts the Borrower straight back on the edge of the next call, so the Bank would be having the same conversation every morning in a falling market. Every published private-bank document opened for this playbook takes the no-fixed-period position, so this is the market opening rather than an aggressive one. Keeping the call itself discretionary matters just as much: the Bank must never be in the position where a failure to send a notice is the reason it cannot enforce.

ladder.text: On a Collateral Shortfall the Bank will notify the Borrower, and the Borrower must restore the Lending Value to the Restoration Level by 5.00 p.m. on the day falling X business days after the notice is given, by repayment or by pledging further Eligible Collateral acceptable to the Bank or both. Within 1 business day of the notice the Borrower must deliver a written statement of how it will meet the Collateral Shortfall. The cure period does not run, and the Bank may act immediately, where the Lending Value has fallen below Z per cent of the amounts outstanding (the Hard Floor), where an Event of Default has occurred and is continuing, or where the Bank determines that the market value or the traded liquidity of the pledged assets is declining rapidly. Where a further Collateral Shortfall arises while an earlier one is uncured, the time to cure the further shortfall ends on the later of the cure time then running and 5.00 p.m. on the first business day after notice of it. Restoration is measured on the values determined by the Bank on the date of the notice. Expiry of the cure period is an Event of Default; any notice required under the enforcement clause runs from that expiry and is not additional to the cure period.
ladder.rationale: This tier concedes the clock and keeps everything the clock is for. A defined, short period is easier to operate than a bare demand right, because the relationship manager, the credit officer and the Borrower all know which day the position closes, and the Bank can evidence a fair process if it is ever challenged on the sale. The written statement inside one business day is the cheapest protection in the clause: it tells the Bank on day one whether the money exists, so a cure that is never going to happen is identified before the period runs rather than after. The Hard Floor is not really a concession at all - below it the collateral is no longer covering the debt on any view, and a cure period at that point funds the Borrower's option at the Bank's expense.

ladder.text: Where, on or before the expiry of the cure period, the Borrower delivers a written cure plan identifying the source of the funds, the steps required to release them and the date on which they will be received, and the Bank is satisfied that the source is identified and committed, the Bank may extend the cure period to the date falling X plus N business days after the original notice. During any extension the Bank will not realise the pledged assets by reason only of the Collateral Shortfall to which the plan relates. The extension terminates immediately and without notice if: the Lending Value falls below the Hard Floor; a further Collateral Shortfall arises; any step in the cure plan is not completed by the date given for it; an Event of Default occurs; or the Bank determines that the market value or the traded liquidity of the pledged assets is declining rapidly. A sale of pledged assets instructed by the Borrower counts as a cure only from delivery of executed trade confirmations before the cure time, with the proceeds paid to the Bank on settlement. An extension granted under this clause does not extend, and is not additional to, any notice period under the enforcement clause, and does not affect the Bank's right to realise without notice in the circumstances that clause preserves.
ladder.rationale: The honest case for this tier is that a cure plan with a real funding source is worth more to the Bank than a liquidation into a falling market, and the institutional documents that concede an extension all concede it in the same shape: a standstill bought with information, not with time. What the Bank must not do is turn that into a free option, which is why the extension collapses on any one of five events rather than running to its stated end. Said out loud to a counterparty, the Bank will wait for money it can see and will not wait for money it is being told about. Note that the Bank still declines to be cured by additional securities in this tier, because pledging more of a portfolio that is already falling changes the size of the problem and not its direction.
conditions: Collateral is diversified within the concentration limit and is exchange-listed or daily-dealt.
No line of the portfolio is issuer-restricted, locked up or subject to a trading suspension.
The Bank or a member of its group is the Custodian, or an executed account control agreement is in place.
The funding source named in the cure plan is identified, committed and independent of the pledged portfolio.
The facility is not already in default for any other reason, and no earlier extension has been granted on the same shortfall.
Credit has confirmed that the extension is priced into the lending values applied to this portfolio.

ladder.text: The Bank will not agree that a margin call, a notice or the expiry of a cure period is a condition precedent to enforcement in all cases; will not agree a cure period that continues to run after the Lending Value has fallen below the Hard Floor, after an Event of Default, or through a rapid decline in value or liquidity; will not accept restoration only to the Trigger Level; will not accept cure by the pledge of additional securities of the same issuer, sector or currency as the position causing the shortfall, or by unexecuted instructions or an undertaking to sell; will not give up the anti-stacking rule so that each fresh shortfall carries a fresh full period; and will not accept a cure period that runs cumulatively with, or that suspends, the notice period under the enforcement clause.
ladder.rationale: Each of these turns a protection into a delay, and the delay always lands on the worst day. A cure period that is a precondition to enforcement in all cases means a single failed notice costs the Bank the position. Stacked cure periods are the subtler version of the same problem: in a market that falls every day, a fresh full period on every fresh shortfall is an indefinite standstill granted by arithmetic. Restoration to the Trigger Level is refused in every document opened for this playbook, which is the shortest available answer if the point is pressed in the room.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: The published Luxembourg documents are the two poles of this clause. One states no cure period at all - notification on a best-endeavours basis only, at the bank's sole discretion, creating no client right, with amounts due immediately and any deferral a discretionary favour (BANK-LU-01). The other is the only bank-terms document opened with two numeric levels, calling for further cover once the lendable exchange value falls below 130 per cent of outstandings and permitting realisation of part or all of the pledge straight away and without any notice below 120 per cent (BANK-LU-02) - which is exactly the Trigger Level and Hard Floor architecture used above, and a useful answer to a counterparty who says the Hard Floor is invented. Keep the cure period in the facility letter and out of the security agreement: enforcement without prior notice is the statutory default under the Law of 5 August 2005 only "unless otherwise provided for", so a cure period drafted into the security document narrows the statutory enforcement power itself (LAW-LU-01, art. 11(1)).
escalation_triggers: Any request for a cure period longer than X business days, or for more than one extension on the same shortfall.
Any request that a cure period continue to run below the Hard Floor, during a rapid decline, or after an Event of Default.
Any request that notice of a margin call be a condition precedent to enforcement.
Any request to restore only to the Trigger Level, or to measure restoration on a moving price rather than on the price on the notice date.
Any request to cure by pledging additional securities rather than by cash or repayment.
Any request to remove the anti-stacking rule.
Any request that the cure period and the enforcement notice period run cumulatively.
not_automated: Whether to grant forbearance on a live margin call, or to let an expired cure period stand without enforcing.
Whether a written cure plan is credible, which is a judgement about a funding source and not a document check.
Setting the Trigger Level, the Restoration Level, the Hard Floor and the number of business days. The sources give a band, not an answer.
Whether a particular market move is a "rapid decline" that stops the cure clock.
Whether to call at all on a relationship where the shortfall is small and the portfolio is recovering.

clauses.title: Security structure: pledge, charge or title transfer, plus control and custody
clauses.opening_text: The Pledgor grants to the Bank a first-ranking and continuing security interest over each Collateral Account, over all financial instruments and cash from time to time credited to it, over all rights attaching to them and over all proceeds, present and future, taking the form the Bank determines to be most effective under the law of the place where the Collateral Account is maintained, and the Pledgor will execute any further document and give any further instruction the Bank requires for that purpose. The Bank or a member of its group is the Custodian. No financial instrument or cash may be withdrawn, transferred, sold, substituted or otherwise dealt with, and no instruction to the Custodian is effective, without the Bank's prior consent, which the Bank may withhold; the Bank may release only such assets as it determines to be in excess of its requirements, taking lending values, currency exposure, tax and any other risk into account. The Pledgor will create no other security interest over, and will permit no filing, registration or notice in respect of, any Collateral Account or any asset credited to it, will defend the collateral against any adverse claim, and will bear the Bank's costs of perfecting, defending and enforcing the security. Voting and other rights attaching to the collateral are exercisable by the Pledgor only until the Bank gives notice, after which they are exercisable by the Bank or its nominee under an irrevocable power of attorney given by the Pledgor. The Bank reserves the right to use, transfer or dispose of the collateral to the extent permitted by the applicable law and any authorisation given by the Pledgor.
clauses.opening_rationale: What makes this product lendable is not the security document, it is that the Bank is holding the assets and can stop them moving. Where the Bank is the Custodian the structure is at its cheapest and its fastest in all three jurisdictions in this playbook: the pledge agreement alone perfects in Luxembourg, an agreement with the custodian alone does it in Switzerland, and in England the possession-or-control question answers itself. Full dominion with releases in the Bank's gift is also the observed private-bank position rather than an aggressive one. The reason to open here and not one tier down is that every concession in this clause is a concession about who can move an asset on the morning of a default, and that is the one question the Bank cannot afford to have argued about on the day.
