ladder.text: The security is a pledge or charge and not a transfer of title. The collateral may be held by a Custodian other than the Bank only where, as a condition precedent, the Bank has received an executed control agreement between the Pledgor, the Custodian and the Bank under which the Custodian agrees to act on the Bank's instructions in relation to the Collateral Account without any further consent or cooperation from the Pledgor, and subordinates or waives its own liens, rights of retention, rights of use and rights of set-off over the Collateral Account. The Pledgor may give instructions in respect of the Collateral Account, and may sell and reinvest within it, until the Bank gives a blocking notice to the Custodian; no asset may leave the Collateral Account and no cash may be withdrawn from it without the Bank's consent, other than proceeds reinvested in Eligible Collateral within the applicable limits. The Bank will not use, lend, re-pledge or otherwise dispose of the collateral before an Event of Default except as the security documents permit or as the Pledgor has authorised in writing. Voting and corporate action rights remain with the Pledgor until an Event of Default, after which they vest in the Bank under an irrevocable power of attorney. The Bank may give a blocking notice at any time after an Event of Default or a Collateral Shortfall, and will confirm the release of the notice in writing once the cause has been remedied.
ladder.rationale: Two of the three things conceded here are conceded in the filed institutional documents as well, so the Bank is not moving off market: no reuse before default, and voting left with the client until default. Neither costs the Bank anything it actually needs, and the irrevocable power of attorney means the voting concession reverses exactly when it would start to matter. The real concession is third-party custody, and the answer to it is documentary rather than positional: a control agreement that switches the Custodian's obedience from the client to the Bank, and that deals with the Custodian's own liens, delivers the same practical control as being the Custodian. Making that agreement a condition precedent rather than a post-closing undertaking is the whole point: an unexecuted control agreement is not a slower version of control, it is no control at all.
conditions: The Custodian is a regulated institution in a jurisdiction where local counsel has confirmed the perfection route.
The executed control agreement, and any acknowledgement required by local law, are conditions precedent to first drawing.
Statements and valuations are delivered by the Custodian direct to the Bank.

ladder.text: Where the Pledgor's Custodian will not enter into a tripartite control agreement, the Bank may accept a pledge or charge notified to the Custodian together with the Custodian's written acknowledgement, to be delivered within X business days of the notice, confirming that it holds the Collateral Account subject to the Bank's security, that it will act on the Bank's instructions in relation to the Collateral Account without any further consent from the Pledgor, and that it subordinates its own liens, rights of retention and rights of set-off, in each case only where local counsel has confirmed in writing that this constitutes an effective and enforceable security interest under the law of the place where the Collateral Account is maintained. The Pledgor may substitute Eligible Collateral without the Bank's prior consent up to an aggregate of Y per cent of the Lending Value in any calendar month, provided that after the substitution the portfolio remains within the eligible collateral and concentration limits and the Lending Value is not reduced, and the Bank may withdraw that permission at any time. The Bank will give a blocking notice only on an Event of Default or a Collateral Shortfall. The security remains a security interest over all present and future assets credited to the Collateral Account, and the Bank's rights on enforcement are not conditional on any act, consent or cooperation of the Pledgor or of the Custodian beyond the acknowledgement given.
ladder.rationale: This tier exists because the client's existing custody relationship is often the real obstacle to the trade, and refusing it outright loses business the Bank could safely write. What is conceded is the form of the custodian's agreement and the friction of case-by-case substitution consents; what is not conceded is the substance, which is that on a default the Bank instructs and the Custodian obeys. The local counsel confirmation is doing the load-bearing work, because whether this structure is worth anything is a question of the law of the account's location and nothing else: in Luxembourg a notified two-party pledge plus acknowledgement is an express statutory route, and the client's retained trading rights do not undermine the pledge; in England the courts have required real dispossession of the provider, so the same paper may not deliver control. The honest way to put this to a counterparty is that the Bank is flexible about the mechanism and not about the outcome.
conditions: Local counsel in the place the Collateral Account is maintained has confirmed the structure in writing.
The Custodian is a regulated institution and is not an affiliate of the Borrower or the Pledgor.
The Custodian's acknowledgement is received before first drawing, and its liens are subordinated or waived.
The portfolio is exchange-listed or daily-dealt and is within the concentration limit.
Daily position and valuation reporting is received direct from the Custodian.
No line of the portfolio is issuer-restricted, locked up or subject to a transfer restriction.

ladder.text: The Bank will not take a structure whose perfection, or whose enforcement, depends on an act, consent, instruction or cooperation of the Pledgor, the Borrower or any affiliate of theirs at the time of enforcement; will not accept a Custodian that reserves the right to require the Pledgor's consent before acting on the Bank's instructions, or that will not subordinate or waive its own liens, rights of retention, rights of use and rights of set-off; will not proceed where no route to an effective security interest under the law of the place the Collateral Account is maintained has been identified and confirmed; will not accept a negative pledge, an undertaking not to dispose, or a letter of comfort in place of a security interest; will not accept a transfer of title for security purposes with a client whose classification makes that structure prohibited or voidable in the booking jurisdiction; will not accept release of collateral on the Pledgor's calculation of excess rather than the Bank's; and will not limit the security to a named, static list of holdings in a portfolio the client continues to trade.
ladder.rationale: Every item on this list is a way of ending up with a document that reads like security and behaves like an unsecured loan on the only day it matters. A custodian that needs the client's consent before acting gives the client a veto over enforcement; a structure that has not been confirmed under the law of the account's location is an assumption, not an interest; and a static list over a traded portfolio starts drifting out of date the week after signing. The title transfer point is not a negotiating position at all - in Luxembourg a transfer of title for security purposes with a retail client is prohibited on pain of nullity, so agreeing to it would produce a structure that is void rather than merely weak.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: Luxembourg is the most collateral-taker-friendly of the three on structure, and the one with a hard statutory prohibition in it. The Law of 5 August 2005 allows an all-present-and-future pledge without specific designation of the collateral (art. 4), which is what a revolving Lombard portfolio needs, and expressly provides that a right of substitution, a right to withdraw excess collateral, a right to collect proceeds until further notice and a reserved right of the provider to give instructions do not prejudice the collateral having been provided (art. 2(3)) - so the client can keep trading the portfolio without undermining the pledge, which English law does not allow as freely. Possession is defined functionally: where the Bank is the Custodian, concluding the pledge agreement is enough; otherwise a tripartite agreement, or a two-party agreement notified to the Custodian under which it acts on the Bank's instructions without further agreement of the provider, or booking to the Bank's account, or earmarking in the Custodian's books (art. 5(2)(a)), with routes other than the first treated as a waiver of the Custodian's own ranking unless otherwise agreed. There are no registration formalities (art. 26). The prohibition: a credit institution or investment firm providing investment services may not conclude a transfer of title for security purposes with a retail client, on pain of nullity, and must in any event document its consideration of the use of title transfer (art. 13 and art. 13-1). For a retail-classified Luxembourg client the structural choice is therefore pledge, and the point is not negotiable (LAW-LU-01).
notes: [R12_third_party_custodian] Where the lender does not hold the account, control is whatever the custodian agrees to plus whatever the law governing the securities account requires, and the three playbook jurisdictions answer that differently. English law asks whether the collateral is in the taker's possession or under its control, which turns on real dispossession of the provider. Swiss law on intermediated securities gives three routes to third-party effectiveness, including a control agreement with the custodian and an agreement with the custodian itself. The Luxembourg collateral law lets possession be constituted through an agreed third-party holder, who must then transfer on notice of an enforcement event without the provider's consent. Read the jurisdiction overlay printed with this markup before settling the structure, and confirm with local counsel.
escalation_triggers: Any request that the Bank rely on a security interest over a Collateral Account in a jurisdiction where the perfection route has not been confirmed by local counsel.
Any request that the Custodian retain the right to seek the Pledgor's consent before acting on the Bank's instructions.
Any request that the Custodian keep its own lien, right of retention, right of use or right of set-off ahead of, or equal with, the Bank's security.
Any request for a transfer of title for security purposes where the Pledgor is, or may be, a retail-classified or natural-person client.
Any request for substitution or withdrawal rights beyond Y per cent of the Lending Value in a month, or for release on the Pledgor's own calculation of excess.
Any request to limit the security to named holdings, or to exclude future assets, proceeds or joint accounts.
Any request that the Bank give up the irrevocable power of attorney or the right to vote after an Event of Default.
not_automated: Whether a particular custodian's standard control agreement actually delivers control under the law of the account's location. The tool prints the question; local counsel answers it.
Whether to accept a client's existing custody relationship at all, which is a relationship decision as much as a credit one.
The classification of the client that determines whether title transfer is available in the booking jurisdiction.
Whether to register a charge protectively for a corporate chargor where reliance on the financial collateral regime is doubtful.
Setting the substitution threshold and the acknowledgement deadline. No opened source publishes either.

clauses.title: Events of default, including insolvency, death or incapacity and material adverse change
clauses.opening_text: Each of the following is an Event of Default. The Borrower fails to pay any amount when due. The Borrower or the Pledgor fails to meet a margin call, to deliver additional collateral by the deadline set under the margin maintenance and cure clause, or to respond to a call. Any representation, warranty or information given by or on behalf of a Relevant Person is incorrect, incomplete or misleading when given or when repeated. A Relevant Person is subject to, or is threatened with, insolvency, bankruptcy, moratorium, composition, business failure, material litigation or the appointment of an insolvency officer, or takes any step towards any of them. A Relevant Person who is an individual dies or loses legal capacity, or a Relevant Person which is not an individual is dissolved, ceases to exist, loses a constitutive status on which the facility was granted, or has its constitutive documents amended, restated, revoked or invalidated. Any attachment, seizure, forfeiture, freezing or restraint order, subpoena, court order or regulatory proceeding affects a Relevant Person or a substantial part of its assets. The Bank considers that the collateral has become inadequate, impaired or insecure, or that the conditions on which the Bank granted the facility have changed. An event of default, termination event or acceleration occurs under any other facility, guarantee, hedging or derivative arrangement between a Relevant Person and the Bank or any member of the Bank's group, or under any financial indebtedness of a Relevant Person owed to any other person. Performance becomes unlawful, or a change in law, regulation or regulatory requirement increases the Bank's cost or reduces its return. The security ceases to be a valid, first-ranking and perfected interest in the collateral. "Relevant Person" means the Borrower, the Pledgor, any guarantor, any other provider of collateral, and any beneficial owner or settlor of any of them. On an Event of Default all amounts owing become immediately due and payable without notice or demand, the Bank's commitment (if any) is cancelled, and the Bank may enforce under the security documents without further notice.
clauses.opening_rationale: This list is the Bank's exit, and on this product the exit has to be available before the loss has crystallised rather than after. That is why the insolvency and deterioration limbs reach threatened events: by the time a private client's insolvency is a matter of record, the collateral has usually already moved. The width of "Relevant Person" is deliberate and is the single most contested definition in the clause; a facility to a trust or a personal holding vehicle is in practice a facility to the individual behind it, and the events that damage the credit are events in that individual's life, not in the vehicle's. Every limb here is observed in a published or filed document from this side of the market, so it is an opening position and not an aggressive one.

ladder.text: Each of the following is an Event of Default. The Borrower fails to pay principal when due, with no grace period, or fails to pay interest, fees or expenses within X business days of the due date. The Borrower or the Pledgor fails to meet a margin call or to deliver additional collateral by the deadline set under the margin maintenance and cure clause, with no grace period and subject to no materiality qualifier. A representation, warranty or information given by or on behalf of a Relevant Person is incorrect or misleading in any material respect when given or repeated. A Relevant Person commences or consents to insolvency, bankruptcy, moratorium or composition proceedings, or has such proceedings commenced against it which are not dismissed or stayed within X days, or is threatened with insolvency in a manner the Bank determines, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner, to be material. A Relevant Person who is an individual dies or loses legal capacity, or a Relevant Person which is not an individual is dissolved or has its constitutive documents revoked or invalidated. The Bank determines, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner, that the collateral has become inadequate or impaired, that the realisable value or the traded liquidity of the collateral has materially deteriorated, or that there has been a substantial deterioration in the financial condition of a Relevant Person. An event of default, termination event or acceleration occurs under any other facility, guarantee, hedging or derivative arrangement between a Relevant Person and the Bank or any member of the Bank's group, or under financial indebtedness of a Relevant Person owed to any other person in an aggregate amount of at least X. Performance becomes unlawful, or the security ceases to be a valid, first-ranking and perfected interest in the collateral. "Relevant Person" means the Borrower, the Pledgor, any guarantor, any other provider of collateral, and any individual whose death or incapacity would, in the Bank's reasonable opinion, affect the ability of the Borrower or the Pledgor to perform or the Bank's ability to deal with the collateral, including a settlor with reserved powers, a sole trustee or a joint account holder. On an Event of Default all amounts owing become immediately due and payable and the Bank may enforce under the security documents; acceleration is automatic and requires no notice where a Relevant Person has itself commenced insolvency proceedings.
ladder.rationale: What moves in this tier is the standard and the calendar, not the list of events. Grace on interest and fees is an operational concession about payment plumbing and it costs the Bank nothing; grace on principal or on a margin call amount would be a different thing entirely, because the margin call has already had its cure period and a second grace period is simply a longer cure. Binding the deterioration and collateral limbs to good faith and commercial reasonableness gives the counterparty an objective standard without giving it a veto, and the filed institutional documents show that standard is where this market actually settles. The narrowed "Relevant Person" definition is drawn by function rather than by status: the question the Bank cares about is whose death or incapacity would stop the collateral being dealt with, and that is a question with a factual answer at intake.

ladder.text: The word "threatened" is deleted from every limb. A breach of any undertaking other than a payment obligation, a margin obligation or a security undertaking is an Event of Default only if it is not remedied within X days of the earlier of notice from the Bank and the date a responsible officer of the Borrower became aware of it, except where the breach by its nature cannot be remedied. The Bank's general determination that the collateral has become inadequate or impaired is replaced by the following events, each of which is an Event of Default: the insolvency of an issuer of a pledged security; a change of control of the Borrower or the Pledgor, meaning the acquisition of more than X per cent of its voting rights or economic interest; the delisting of a pledged security; a suspension of trading in a pledged security continuing for more than X consecutive trading days; the nationalisation or expropriation of an issuer of a pledged security; and any determination by the Bank, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner, that the realisable value or the traded liquidity of the collateral has materially deteriorated. Where an Event of Default arises only from a change in law, regulation or regulatory requirement that increases the Bank's cost or reduces its return, the Bank will give X calendar days' notice before realising collateral. Where a Relevant Person who is an individual dies, the Bank will not realise collateral for X business days from the date it is notified of the death, provided throughout that period that no margin call is outstanding, that the lending value of the collateral is not less than the amounts outstanding, and that the personal representatives or attorneys of the deceased engage with the Bank. Nothing in this tier limits the Bank's right to accelerate on non-payment, on a failure to meet a margin call, on insolvency, on death or loss of capacity, or on the security ceasing to be valid, first-ranking and perfected; and on an uncommitted facility nothing in this clause affects the Bank's right to demand repayment at any time without an Event of Default having occurred.
ladder.rationale: This tier trades the open-ended material adverse change limb for a list, which is the trade the institutional market has already made, and the Bank can point at that when it is accused of being unreasonable. The list is only safe because the Bank keeps a residual limb tied to realisable value and liquidity: the events that actually damage a Lombard book show up in price and liquidity behaviour well before anything anyone has enumerated has happened. The death standstill is the concession that reads worst on paper and is the easiest to live with in practice, because it is conditioned on the position being inside its limits throughout; the moment a call is open, the standstill stops. Note the asymmetry the Bank is relying on here: on an uncommitted facility none of this matters very much, because the Bank can demand repayment without needing a default at all. That is exactly why this tier is not available once the facility is committed, and why the rules close the floor to acceptable on a committed term deal.
conditions: The facility is uncommitted and repayable on demand, so the events of default are not the Bank's only exit.
Collateral is exchange-listed or daily-dealt, diversified within the concentration limit, and priced at least daily.
The Bank or a member of its group is the Custodian, or an executed account control agreement is in place.
There is no third-party pledgor who is an individual, or the death standstill has been excluded for that pledgor.
The Borrower has no other facilities with the Bank or its group that would be prejudiced by the longer cure and standstill periods.
Credit has confirmed the standstill and cure periods are acceptable on this collateral pool.

ladder.text: The Bank will not accept a grace period, a cure period or a materiality qualifier on the failure to meet a margin call or to deliver additional collateral, because that failure is already the output of a cure period; will not accept a grace period on principal; will not delete the general deterioration limb without an enumerated substitute that includes a residual limb tied to the realisable value and liquidity of the collateral; will not remove death of an individual Borrower, Pledgor or guarantor as an Event of Default, nor accept a standstill that continues while a margin call is outstanding or while the lending value is below the amounts outstanding; will not remove loss of legal capacity as an Event of Default where the Borrower or the Pledgor is an individual; will not make the occurrence of an Event of Default, or the exercise of any right following one, conditional on the consent of the Borrower or the Pledgor, on agreement with an estate or its representatives, or on a determination by a third party or a court; will not accept that acceleration requires the Bank to prove loss or to show that the event has had a quantified adverse effect; and will not exclude other facilities, guarantees or hedging arrangements between a Relevant Person and the Bank or its group from the cross-default limb.
ladder.rationale: Each of these turns the list from a right the Bank already holds into an argument the Bank has to win, and the argument always falls due on the day the collateral is falling. A grace period on a margin call is the clearest example: the cure period is the grace period, and adding a second one simply moves the liquidation to a worse price. Removing death or incapacity is the private-wealth version of the same problem, because the person who can give instructions and the person whose assets secure the facility are usually the same person, and when that person is gone the Bank is holding collateral that nobody can lawfully tell it what to do with. Cross-default inside the Bank's own group is non-negotiable for a different reason: the Bank cannot run a relationship in which it is accelerating under one document and forbearing under another.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: Luxembourg is the most favourable of the three on exactly the point that worries a private bank. The financial collateral law applies whether the arrangement is entered into by a merchant or a non-merchant, so an individual pledgor is inside the regime rather than outside it; the arrangements, the agreed enforcement events and the agreed valuation and enforcement measures are effective against third parties, commissioners, receivers and liquidators notwithstanding domestic or foreign reorganisation or winding-up proceedings; and the same rules are stated to apply on the death or incapacity of the collateral provider or the debtor (LAW-LU-01, arts. 2(1) and 20(4)). The one carve-out is the over-indebtedness procedure for private individuals, which is excepted from the general disapplication of insolvency law, so full insolvency remoteness cannot be assumed against a Luxembourg-resident individual. At the commercial end, a published Luxembourg template treats the death of the client as a free-standing ground for unilateral realisation without prior notice and carries a deterioration limb reaching loss of market confidence (BANK-LU-01), so a Luxembourg counterparty is not well placed to argue that the preferred position on death is off-market.
notes: [R03a_natural_person_borrower_no_declaration] Where the borrower is an individual, death and incapacity need to be handled expressly rather than left to the insolvency wording. Say what happens to the facility, who the lender may deal with, and whether the portfolio is frozen or may be liquidated in the meantime.
escalation_triggers: Any request for a grace period, cure period or materiality qualifier on the margin call limb or on principal.
Any request to delete the material adverse change limb without an enumerated substitute, or to delete the residual value-and-liquidity limb from that substitute.
Any request for a payment grace period longer than X business days, or a general covenant cure longer than X days.
Any request to remove death or loss of capacity of an individual Borrower, Pledgor or guarantor, or for a standstill on death longer than X business days or one that survives an open margin call.
Any request to narrow "Relevant Person" so that it no longer reaches an individual whose death or incapacity would affect the ability to deal with the collateral.
Any request to exclude other facilities with the Bank or its group from the cross-default limb.
Any counterparty request on this clause where the facility is committed rather than repayable on demand.
not_automated: Whether a material adverse change or a substantial deterioration has actually occurred on a live position. The clause fixes who decides and on what standard; it does not decide.
Whether to call a default at all, as against forbearing while the relationship is discussed. Forbearance on a live margin call and waiver of an event of default are both human decisions.

Whether an individual has lost legal capacity, and whether an attorney, deputy or other representative can give instructions that bind the Borrower or the Pledgor. [VERIFY] no mental-capacity source was opened for this playbook.
Whether to enforce against a deceased individual's collateral before the estate is administered, which is a reputational and conduct decision as much as a legal one.

clauses.title: Enforcement and liquidation: notice, standard of conduct and self-help sale
clauses.opening_text: On an Event of Default the Bank may, without demand, advertisement or notice of intention, all of which the Pledgor waives to the fullest extent permitted by law, take control of the Collateral Account and of all proceeds, transfer the collateral into its own name or that of a nominee, sell or otherwise dispose of all or any part of the collateral publicly or privately, at such time, place, price, in such order and on such terms as the Bank determines, and apply the proceeds against the secured obligations in such order as the Bank determines. Where notice is required by law and may not be waived, the Bank will give such notice as the law requires; no notice is required where the collateral is of a type customarily sold on a recognised market or where the Bank determines that it threatens to decline speedily in value. The Bank may instead appropriate all or any part of the collateral where the applicable law permits, at a value determined in accordance with this agreement. The Pledgor acknowledges that the Bank is not obliged to sell in tranches or over any period, to seek any strategic buyer or any control premium, to delay a sale in order to obtain a better price, or to sell at all after giving any notice, and that a sale may be at a material discount. The Pledgor remains liable for any shortfall after application of the proceeds, together with the Bank's costs of enforcement.
clauses.opening_rationale: The value of this clause is measured in hours. A portfolio that can be sold on the day of default is worth its market price; a portfolio that can be sold in a week is worth whatever the market does in that week, and the Bank did not price that risk. The pre-agreed acknowledgements are the most useful drafting in the whole pool and they are worth explaining rather than just inserting: the dispute after an enforcement is almost never about whether the Bank could sell, it is about whether it should have sold differently, and these acknowledgements answer that question in advance in the Pledgor's own words. The recognised-market carve-out is not a trick either - for a listed portfolio it is simply accurate, which is why every private-bank document opened for this playbook concedes a notice period and then removes it in the same breath for the collateral this product is secured on.

ladder.text: On an Event of Default the Bank may sell or otherwise dispose of all or any part of the collateral publicly or privately, or appropriate it where the applicable law permits, in each case acting in a commercially reasonable manner and applying the proceeds against the secured obligations. Where notice of a sale is required by law, the Bank will give the Pledgor not less than X business days' notice of the time and place of a public sale, or of the time after which a private sale may be made, which the Pledgor agrees is reasonable notice; no such notice is required where the collateral is of a type customarily sold on a recognised market, where the Bank determines that it threatens to decline speedily in value, or where giving notice would breach any law, regulation or order applying to the Bank or to the collateral. The Pledgor acknowledges that selling promptly rather than over an extended period, selling without seeking any strategic buyer or control premium, selling at a discount reflecting the size of the holding, effecting a sale by a customary bookbuild, and making a private placement in good faith where a public sale would raise securities law or transfer-restriction issues are each commercially reasonable. The Bank is not obliged to sell after giving notice, may adjourn a sale by announcement without further notice, and the Pledgor remains liable for any shortfall.
ladder.rationale: The move from the Bank's discretion to a commercially reasonable manner costs the Bank very little and buys a lot of goodwill, because what has to be reasonable is the manner of the sale judged objectively and not the result - the English authority on appropriation says so in terms, and the Luxembourg statute writes the same standard into the private-sale route. Keeping the acknowledgements is what makes the concession safe: without them, "commercially reasonable" is an open invitation to argue after the event that the Bank should have waited. This is also the tier the rules drive the floor up to when the deal gets harder, and that is the right way round. Where the Pledgor is an insider of a pledged issuer, or a line is locked up or otherwise restricted, or the portfolio is illiquid, the sale is already going to be slowed by closed periods, issuer or underwriter consents, volume limits or the absence of a daily price - so a universal notice period on top of those delays is precisely the concession the Bank cannot afford, and an enforcement on those facts is also the one most likely to be challenged, which is when the pre-agreed acknowledgements earn their place.

ladder.text: On an Event of Default the Bank will give the Pledgor not less than X business days' notice of the time and place of any public sale of the collateral, or of the time after which any private sale may be made, which the Pledgor agrees is commercially reasonable notice. No such notice is required, and the Bank may sell or appropriate immediately, where the collateral is of a type customarily sold on a recognised market; where the Bank determines that the market value or the traded liquidity of the collateral is declining rapidly; where giving notice would breach any law, regulation or order, or would prejudice the Bank's ability to realise the collateral; or where any insolvency, seizure, freezing or similar process has been commenced or threatened in respect of the Pledgor or the collateral. The Bank will act in a commercially reasonable manner, and the Pledgor acknowledges that the Bank is under no obligation to sell in tranches or over any period, and that a private placement made in good faith where a public sale would raise securities law or transfer-restriction issues is commercially reasonable. The Bank is not obliged to sell after giving notice and may adjourn a sale by announcement. A notice period under this clause runs from the expiry of any cure period under the margin maintenance clause and is not additional to it, and the Pledgor remains liable for any shortfall.
ladder.rationale: This is the concession the counterparty actually wants, and it is survivable only in the shape the private-banking documents give it: a real period for the ordinary case, and immediate realisation for the cases where a period would cause the loss it is meant to prevent. Said plainly across the table, the Bank is agreeing to tell the client before it sells, and not agreeing to stand still while the position gets worse. Note what has and has not moved. The notice period has become universal rather than law-driven, and the list of pre-agreed acknowledgements has been cut back to the two that carry the most weight. What has not moved is the carve-out list, the absence of any obligation to sell, and the deficiency. The sentence tying this period to the margin cure period is not housekeeping - without it a counterparty reads the two clauses together as a single, much longer standstill, which is not what is being agreed.
conditions: The portfolio is exchange-listed or daily-dealt, and no line is issuer-restricted, locked up or subject to a transfer restriction.
No pledgor, borrower or connected person is an insider or a person discharging managerial responsibilities of a pledged issuer.
Collateral is within the concentration limit and the currency of the collateral matches the facility, or an FX haircut has been applied.
The Bank or a member of its group is the Custodian, or an executed account control agreement is in place.
The margin maintenance cure period is at or tighter than its default floor for this deal.
Credit has confirmed the notice period is priced into the lending values applied.

ladder.text: The Bank will not accept a notice period that applies where the collateral is of a type customarily sold on a recognised market, where value or liquidity is falling rapidly, where an insolvency, seizure or freezing process has begun or is threatened, or where giving notice would breach a law or prejudice realisation; will not accept a standstill after an Event of Default, a right to cure after an enforcement notice has been given, or a requirement to act jointly with or wait for another creditor; will not accept an obligation to sell in tranches, to follow a scheduled or volume-weighted programme, to seek strategic buyers or a control premium, or otherwise to maximise rather than realise; will not accept a requirement for a court order, an independent valuation or the Pledgor's consent before appropriating or selling; will not accept non-recourse for any deficiency; and will not agree that a failure to give a notice, or any delay in exercising a remedy, is a waiver of the remedy or of the Event of Default.
ladder.rationale: Each of these converts a self-help remedy into a process the Pledgor or a third party can slow down, and the only time anyone wants to slow an enforcement down is when the collateral is falling. A notice period that survives a rapid decline is not a notice period, it is a free option written by the Bank; an obligation to sell in an orderly programme is the same option with a schedule attached. Non-recourse is refused in every document opened for this playbook, and the reason is worth saying out loud: a deficiency waiver converts a secured loan into a put on the portfolio struck at the loan amount, which is not the product and is not the price.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: Luxembourg is the strongest of the three and the enforcement clause should be drafted to use it rather than to restate it. Article 11(1) of the Law of 5 August 2005 lets the pledgee, unless otherwise provided for and WITHOUT PRIOR NOTICE, appropriate the collateral at a price set by the agreed valuation method, assign it by private sale in a commercially reasonable manner or on a trading venue where it is admitted to trading or by public auction, obtain a judicial attribution against an expert valuation, net, appropriate listed instruments at market price or fund units at the last published net asset value provided it is under a year old, or request redemption of fund units. Article 11(3) obliges an agreed third-party custodian to transfer the instruments on notice of an enforcement event without the provider's consent and without informing it in advance, and article 20 makes the arrangement, the agreed enforcement events and the agreed valuation and enforcement measures effective against insolvency officials notwithstanding reorganisation or winding-up proceedings (LAW-LU-01). Two drafting warnings. Avoid the public auction route unless it is needed: article 11(2) imposes at least eight working days' press notice and minutes within three working days, which is the slowest option on the menu. And because article 11(1) applies only "unless otherwise provided for", a negotiated notice period written into the security agreement narrows the statutory power itself - if a client insists on notice, put it in the facility letter as an undertaking rather than as a condition of the enforcement right. Published Luxembourg bank documents take exactly this position, realising on the exchange or the open market without prior notice (BANK-LU-01, BANK-LU-03) and permitting immediate realisation below the lower cover level (BANK-LU-02).
escalation_triggers: Any request for a notice period longer than X business days before a sale or an appropriation.
Any request to remove or narrow the recognised-market, rapid-decline, unlawful-notice or insolvency-process carve-outs.
Any request for a standstill after an Event of Default, or for a right to cure once an enforcement notice has been given.
Any request for an obligation to sell in an orderly or scheduled manner, or to seek a strategic buyer or a control premium.
Any request for a court order, an independent valuation or the Pledgor's consent as a precondition to appropriation or sale.
Any request for non-recourse, or for a cap on the Pledgor's liability for a deficiency.
Any request to delete the pre-agreed acknowledgements of what is commercially reasonable.
not_automated: The decision to enforce at all, as against forbearing while the relationship is discussed. The tool never makes that call.
Whether a particular market move is a "rapid decline" that removes the notice period.
Whether a proposed sale method is commercially reasonable on the facts of the day, including the choice between a bookbuild, a programme and a private placement.
Whether a closed period, an issuer or underwriter consent or a volume limit blocks or delays a sale, and whether compliance has cleared it.
Whether notice is required by law and unwaivable in the booking jurisdiction, and on whom it must be served where the Pledgor is not the Borrower.
Setting the notice period. Three observations exist across one composite filing, and the number is risk appetite.

clauses.title: Capacity, authority and due execution for trusts, corporates and partnerships
clauses.opening_text: Each of the Borrower and each Pledgor represents and warrants that it is duly constituted and validly existing; that it has the power and authority to enter into and perform the finance documents and to create the security; that every action, consent and authorisation required by its constitutional or trust documents, by any applicable law or by any agreement binding on it, including any shareholder, beneficiary, partner or protector consent, has been taken or obtained and is in full force; that the finance documents have been executed by persons authorised to do so; that its obligations are legal, valid, binding and enforceable; that entry into and performance of them does not conflict with its constitutional or trust documents, any law or any agreement binding on it; and that it is solvent and will not be rendered insolvent by the transaction. Where a party contracts as trustee, it further represents that it is duly appointed and is the sole trustee or is acting with all of its co-trustees; that the trust instrument and every deed of appointment, retirement or variation empower it to borrow, to charge the trust assets and to delegate as contemplated by the finance documents; that it is not acting in breach of trust and has no notice of any claim that it is; and that its right of indemnity out of the trust fund is not excluded, limited or impaired, and it undertakes not to exclude, limit or impair it, not to retire without a replacement trustee acceding to the finance documents, not to distribute or appoint trust property, and not to incur any liability ranking in priority to the Bank's claim on that indemnity, in each case without the Bank's prior written consent. The trustee contracts in both its personal and its trustee capacity and its liability is not limited to the trust fund. Where a party is a partnership, it represents that the borrowing and the security are within the ordinary course of the partnership business or have been authorised by all of the partners, that the partnership agreement permits them, and that each partner is jointly and, where its constitution permits, severally liable, and it undertakes to notify any change in the partners and to procure that any incoming partner accedes. Where a Pledgor is not the Borrower, its obligations are absolute and unconditional irrespective of the validity or enforceability of the Borrower's obligations, any variation of the facility, any release of other collateral or guarantees, or any other circumstance which would otherwise operate as a defence available to a surety, all of which are waived. Each Pledgor which is a company further represents that granting the security is for its corporate benefit as determined by its board and does not constitute unlawful financial assistance. Each representation is repeated on each utilisation date and on each day on which any amount is outstanding, and each of the Borrower and each Pledgor undertakes to notify the Bank immediately of any change in its beneficial owners, trustees, general partner or controllers, any such change being subject to fresh know-your-client review and to the Bank's approval.
clauses.opening_rationale: This clause is the one that decides whether the Bank has security at all, because a pledge granted by someone who lacked the power to grant it is not a weak pledge, it is no pledge. The cost of getting it right is a week of reading documents the client already has; the cost of getting it wrong surfaces on the day the Bank tries to sell, which is the day the beneficiaries or the minority shareholder appear. Full personal recourse against a trustee is the opening position rather than the answer, but it has to be the opening position, because the moment the Bank concedes limited recourse it is relying entirely on the trustee's indemnity and it needs to have asked about that indemnity first. The notification undertaking is the cheapest thing on the list and the most useful: capacity is not a fact about signing day, it is a fact about every day the loan is outstanding.

ladder.text: The trustee's liability under the finance documents is limited to the assets of the trust from time to time and to the trustee's right of indemnity out of them, provided that: the trustee represents that its right of indemnity is not excluded, limited or impaired and that it is not acting in breach of trust; the undertakings not to impair the indemnity, not to retire without a replacement trustee acceding, and not to distribute trust property without the Bank's consent remain in force; the Bank is subrogated to the trustee's right of indemnity and to the trustee's lien over the trust assets; and the limitation does not apply to any liability arising from the trustee's own fraud, wilful default or negligence or from a breach of the representations in this clause, for which the trustee remains personally liable. A representation as to solvency, and a representation that no consent required by an agreement binding on the obligor has been omitted, may be given so far as the obligor is aware having made due enquiry. A Pledgor which is a company may give its corporate benefit representation by reference to the determination recorded in the resolution authorising the security.
ladder.rationale: Limited recourse is a reasonable ask from a professional trustee and it can be agreed, because the trustee is not the credit: the trust fund is, and the Bank has security over it. What the Bank cannot agree to is limited recourse in the abstract, because recourse to the trust fund runs through the trustee's indemnity, and the indemnity is lost precisely when the trustee acted outside its powers or in breach of its duties, which is the same event that would have made the security defective. So the concession and the protection are the same sentence: the Bank will take the trust fund instead of the trustee, provided the route to the trust fund is intact and the trustee stays personally on the hook for telling the truth about it. A knowledge qualifier on solvency is a different kind of concession and a cheap one, because a solvency representation is an opinion in any event and the Bank is not going to run a solvency analysis of a trustee.
conditions: The trustee is a professional or institutional trustee, or a corporate trustee of substance.
The trust instrument has been read and confirms the power to borrow and to charge.
The indemnity representation and the anti-impairment undertakings are given and are not qualified by knowledge.
Personal liability survives for fraud, wilful default, negligence and breach of the capacity representations.

ladder.text: The trustee's liability under the finance documents is limited to the assets of the trust from time to time, and no claim may be made against the trustee personally or against its other assets, except in the case of the trustee's own fraud or wilful default. A Pledgor's authority certificate may be confined to its constitutional documents and to applicable law, excluding any agreement binding on it, where the Bank receives a legal opinion covering the absence of conflict with any such agreement. Where a Pledgor which is an individual is not the Borrower, the confirmation that independent legal advice was given may be delivered as a certificate from that Pledgor's own solicitor, naming the adviser and the date, rather than as a representation in the security document.
ladder.rationale: This is conceded on relationship grounds and it is not free: the Bank is giving up the one lever that makes a trustee careful about what it represents. It only works where something else does the same job, which is why the conditions replace the representation with an opinion from counsel in the trust's own jurisdiction, with consent rights over the things that destroy an indemnity, and with a lower lending value to carry the residual risk. The line to take in the room is that the Bank is not asking the trustee to underwrite the trust, it is asking to be told the truth about the trust, and if the trustee will not stand behind what it says about its own powers then the Bank has to buy that comfort somewhere else and the price is in the advance rate. Note that a limited recourse clause with no carve-out at all for fraud sits in the unacceptable tier, not here.
conditions: An institutional trustee of substance, regulated in its jurisdiction.
A legal opinion from counsel qualified in the law governing the trust, confirming the power to borrow and to charge, due authorisation, and that the trustee's right of indemnity is unimpaired.
The Bank has first-ranking security over the trust assets and is subrogated to the trustee's indemnity and lien.
Consent rights over further borrowing by the trust, over distributions and appointments, and over any change of trustee; notification of any mandatory distribution.
The governing law of the finance documents and the location of the trust assets have been checked against any statutory limited-recourse protection being relied on.
Lending values have been reduced by credit to reflect the loss of personal recourse.

ladder.text: The Bank will not accept recourse limited to the trust fund where the trustee's right of indemnity is excluded, limited or impaired, or where the trustee will not represent that it is unimpaired and that the trustee is not acting in breach of trust; will not accept a limited recourse clause with no carve-out for the trustee's own fraud; will not accept a certificate from a director, trustee or partner in place of the trust instrument, constitutional documents or partnership agreement themselves; will not take security from a company for another person's debt on a director's certificate alone where the pledgor is incorporated in a jurisdiction that restricts financial assistance, upstream or cross-stream security or requires a corporate benefit analysis, without local counsel confirmation; will not accept a signature on behalf of a partnership without evidence that the signing partner is authorised; will not delete the surety-defence waivers given by a third-party pledgor; will not proceed where a third-party pledgor who is an individual has declined independent legal advice; and will not accept the deletion of the undertaking to notify a change of trustee, general partner, controller or beneficial owner.
ladder.rationale: Everything in this list has the same shape: it asks the Bank to take the granting party's word for the one thing that decides whether the security exists. Limited recourse without an indemnity is not security over a trust fund, it is an unsecured claim against a trustee who has already told you it will not pay. A certificate instead of the deed is the same trade, and it fails in the same place, because the person certifying is the person whose authority is in question. The independent advice point is not a formality either: it is the answer the Bank gives years later when a pledgor says they did not understand what they were signing, and there is no substitute for it once the argument has started.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: One authority obstacle is removed by statute at the point it would otherwise bite hardest: shareholder approval is not required to realise a pledge over all the shares of a Luxembourg private limited company granted in a single transaction, and in other cases the approval may be given irrevocably in advance (LAW-LU-01, art. 12). That is worth knowing at signing rather than at enforcement, because it tells the deal team which consents actually have to be collected as conditions precedent. Separately, the published Luxembourg template shows how a booking centre handles authority for a private client largely by representation rather than by document, including a representation that the client acts for its own account and not for third parties with an undertaking to notify immediately on any change of beneficial owner, that change being subject to fresh know-your-client review and formal approval (BANK-LU-01) - which is the model for the notification undertaking in the preferred tier. clauses.title: Governing law, jurisdiction and service of process
clauses.opening_text: The facility letter and any non-contractual obligations arising out of it are governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which the Bank books the facility. The security agreement and any non-contractual obligations arising out of it are governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which the collateral account is maintained, and where that account is maintained in a jurisdiction which permits the applicable law to be chosen in the account agreement, the account agreement expressly designates that same law as governing the proprietary questions relating to the collateral. The Borrower and the Pledgor irrevocably submit to the jurisdiction of the courts of the jurisdiction in which the Bank books the facility, waive any objection on the ground of venue or forum non conveniens, and agree that a judgment of those courts is conclusive and enforceable in any other jurisdiction. That submission is for the benefit of the Bank only: nothing in it limits the Bank's right to bring proceedings, or to seek interim, protective or enforcement relief, in the courts of the jurisdiction in which the collateral account is maintained, in which the Borrower or the Pledgor is domiciled or has assets, or in any other court of competent jurisdiction, and the Bank may bring concurrent proceedings in more than one jurisdiction. Each of the Borrower and the Pledgor which is not resident in the jurisdiction of the Bank's booking location irrevocably appoints a process agent in that jurisdiction to receive service on its behalf, will maintain that appointment for so long as any amount is outstanding, and will appoint a replacement within X days if the appointment ceases to be effective; failure to do so entitles the Bank to appoint a replacement at the Borrower's cost. Each of the Borrower and the Pledgor irrevocably waives, to the fullest extent permitted by law, any immunity from suit, from jurisdiction, from any order for specific performance or recovery of property, and from attachment, execution or other enforcement against its assets, and agrees that it enters into the documents in respect of commercial and not governmental activity.
clauses.opening_rationale: The Bank's opening position is the one every private-bank document opened for this playbook takes: the client submits to one forum, and the Bank keeps the right to go wherever the assets are. That is not greed, it is the shape of the product. Enforcement in this business means getting at a securities account, and the account is wherever the custodian keeps it, which is frequently not where the client is and not where the facility is booked. The split governing law is the point a counterparty most often misses and the Bank should explain rather than trade: in England and in Luxembourg the proprietary questions are assigned by statute to the law of the place where the account is maintained, so governing the security document by some other law does not move the analysis, it just creates a mismatch between the document and the law that will decide the case.

ladder.text: The facility letter is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which the Bank books the facility and the security agreement is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which the collateral account is maintained. The courts of the jurisdiction in which the Bank books the facility have exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute, and the Borrower and the Pledgor waive any objection on the ground of venue or forum non conveniens. Notwithstanding that exclusivity, the Bank may at any time bring proceedings for interim, protective or enforcement relief, and may enforce any judgment, in the courts of the jurisdiction in which the collateral account is maintained or in which the Borrower or the Pledgor has assets, and the Borrower and the Pledgor irrevocably submit to those courts for that purpose. The process agent appointment and the waiver of immunity apply as set out in the preferred position. This clause does not affect the application of any rule of the forum which the parties may not displace by agreement.
ladder.rationale: The concession in this tier is the general right to sue first wherever the Bank likes; what is kept is the right to act where the assets are, which is the part with economic value. A private bank that can seize and sell an account in the jurisdiction where it sits, and enforce its judgment there, has lost very little by agreeing that the merits are heard in one place. Naming the carve-out for interim and protective relief explicitly is also better drafting than relying on a general asymmetry, because it is the limb a counterparty's counsel is least likely to resist and the one most likely to survive a challenge in a forum that dislikes one-sided clauses. The express preservation of mandatory rules of the forum is the Bank's own protection: a clause that overreaches in a consumer or conduct context is the clause most likely to be read down as a whole.

ladder.text: The facility letter is governed by the law of, and the courts of, the jurisdiction agreed between the parties, which may be the jurisdiction in which the Borrower is domiciled or a third jurisdiction, and that jurisdiction is exclusive and mutual. The security agreement remains governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which the collateral account is maintained, and where that jurisdiction permits the applicable law to be chosen in the account agreement, the account agreement continues to designate it. Notwithstanding the mutual and exclusive submission, the Bank may at any time apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for interim, protective or conservatory relief, may take any step required to preserve, perfect or enforce its security or to realise the collateral in the jurisdiction in which the collateral account is maintained, and may enforce any judgment or award in any jurisdiction in which the Borrower or the Pledgor has assets. The process agent appointment and the waiver of immunity are unchanged, and the waiver of immunity is not negotiable where the Borrower or the Pledgor is a trust, a fund, a state or an entity which is or may be entitled to claim immunity. Where the parties agree arbitration instead of litigation, the arbitration clause carves out, and does not require the Bank to exhaust any negotiation period before seeking, interim and protective relief and any step to preserve or realise the collateral.
ladder.rationale: This tier gives away the asymmetry and keeps the two things that decide whether the Bank gets paid: the security document follows the account, and the Bank can always act, immediately and anywhere, to preserve or realise the collateral. Said plainly to a counterparty, the Bank is agreeing to argue about the money in one place of their choosing, and reserving the right to stop the assets moving in whatever place they happen to be. The immunity waiver is held back from this trade deliberately: where a trust, a fund or a state-linked vehicle is the borrower or the pledgor, the immunity point is not a boilerplate courtesy but the difference between a judgment and a recovery. Note also that the drafting concession here is smaller than it looks in two of the three jurisdictions, because the proprietary law is assigned by statute and the parties could not have chosen it anyway.
conditions: The agreed forum is one in which the Bank's counsel confirms a money judgment can be obtained and enforced against the Borrower's assets.

ladder.text: The Bank will not agree that the security agreement is governed by a law other than that of the jurisdiction in which the collateral account is maintained, or that the choice of law in the facility letter determines the proprietary questions which the law of the account's location assigns to itself; will not accept an exclusive forum in which the Bank cannot obtain interim or protective relief, or from which it cannot realise or enforce against the collateral account; will not give up the right to apply for interim, protective or conservatory relief, or to take steps to preserve or realise the collateral, in any jurisdiction; will not accept an arbitration clause without that carve-out, or one which requires a negotiation or cooling-off period to expire before the Bank may act against the collateral; will not delete the waiver of immunity where the Borrower or the Pledgor is a trust, a fund, a state, a state agency or any entity which is or may become entitled to claim immunity from suit or execution; and will not proceed without a process agent, or with service permitted only at an address outside the agreed forum, where the Borrower or the Pledgor is not resident in that forum.
ladder.rationale: Each of these is a way of separating the Bank's rights from the place where the assets are, and the whole design of a securities-backed facility is that those two things stay together. A forum that cannot give interim relief is a forum in which the client can move or dissipate the collateral faster than the Bank can be heard. An arbitration clause with a negotiation window and no carve-out is worse: it converts a falling market into a waiting period. The immunity point is the one most often treated as boilerplate and most expensive when it is wrong, because a trust or fund vehicle that can claim immunity from execution turns a judgment into a piece of paper. And a missing process agent does not lose the case, it just adds months to it, which on this product is the same thing.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: Luxembourg mirrors England on the conflicts rule and differs from it on everything else. Article 23 of the 2005 Law is a PRIMA rule covering the legal nature and proprietary effects, the requirements for provision and third-party effectiveness, extinction or subordination by a competing interest or good-faith acquisition, the custodian's obligations to a competing claimant, the conditions for realisation after an enforcement event, and the extent of the arrangement over income and proceeds, all governed by the domestic law of the country where the relevant account is maintained with renvoi excluded; and the relevant account may be one maintained by the collateral taker itself (LAW-LU-01, arts. 1(3) and 23). Luxembourg is not a party to the 2006 Hague Convention (HCCH-SEC-CONV-2006 status table), so there is no account-agreement route around that. What makes Luxembourg law worth choosing for the security is arts. 18-20: the netting, the agreed enforcement events and the agreed valuation and enforcement measures are effective against third parties, commissioners, receivers and liquidators notwithstanding domestic or foreign reorganisation or winding-up proceedings (LAW-LU-01). The observed market drafting matches the preferred position here: a published Luxembourg template chooses Luxembourg law and names the 2005 Law as the statute it relies on, makes Luxembourg the sole place of performance, of debt collection for clients domiciled abroad and of jurisdiction, and then reserves the bank's right to sue at the client's domicile or before any other competent authority with Luxembourg law still applying exclusively, all expressly subject to mandatory conflicts rules (BANK-LU-01).

clauses.title: No advice, non-reliance and risk acknowledgement
clauses.opening_text: Each of the Borrower and the Pledgor represents and acknowledges that it enters into the facility and the security documents on the basis of its own independent analysis and judgement and of such independent advice as it has thought fit to obtain, and is not relying on any statement, representation or assurance by the Bank as to the facility, the documents, the collateral, its value, liquidity or condition, or any other matter. The Bank acts on an execution-only basis in relation to the facility. The Bank gives no investment, tax, legal, accounting or regulatory advice in connection with the facility, makes no recommendation to borrow, to borrow any particular amount, to pledge any particular asset, or to acquire, retain or dispose of any asset, and expresses no view on whether the facility or any resulting position is suitable or appropriate for the Borrower or the Pledgor. Each of the Borrower and the Pledgor further represents that it has the knowledge and experience necessary to evaluate a facility of this kind and the instruments comprising the collateral; that it has access to, and the knowledge to use, the analytical tools needed to evaluate the collateral and the effect of the facility on its portfolio as a whole; and that it has the financial resources and liquidity to bear all the risks of the facility, including the loss of the entire value of the collateral and liability for any shortfall after realisation. Each acknowledges that it has received and read the Bank's risk disclosures; that borrowing against a portfolio magnifies gains and losses and that losses may exceed the amounts deposited; that a fall in value or a change in lending values may require immediate repayment or the delivery of further collateral; that the Bank may realise collateral at a time and on terms that are not of the Borrower's choosing; and that where the facility is in a different currency from the collateral, the currency exposure is the Borrower's. These representations are repeated on each drawing and on each day on which any amount is outstanding.
clauses.opening_rationale: This clause is not there to win an argument after the event; it is there to record what actually happened, which is that the client decided to borrow against its own portfolio. The sophisticated-investor limbs are worth keeping in full because each does different work: the knowledge limb answers "did you understand it", the analytical-tools limb answers "did you model it against the whole portfolio", and the ability-to-bear-loss limb is the only one that answers the question a regulator actually asks, which is whether the client could survive the downside. Execution-only is stated affirmatively rather than by implication, because both of the conduct regimes in scope treat an execution-only relationship differently from an advised one, and the Bank should be saying which one it is in. Every limb here is observed in a filed or published document from this side of the market.

Where the Bank or any member of its group provides investment advice or portfolio management in respect of any account in which collateral is held, the Borrower and the Pledgor acknowledge that the Bank's dual role as lender and as adviser or manager may give rise to a conflict of interest, and consent to the Bank acting in both capacities; that acknowledgement and consent are given in addition to, and do not displace, the Bank's duties in that other capacity. The sophisticated-investor limbs are given by reference to the Borrower's and the Pledgor's actual knowledge and experience at the date of the facility letter, and are repeated only on each drawing. Nothing in this clause limits or excludes any duty, obligation or liability of the Bank under any applicable law or regulation which may not be limited or excluded, and nothing in it is to be read as a statement by the Bank that it has not provided a service which it has in fact provided.
ladder.rationale: This is where the Bank protects itself by conceding. A non-reliance clause that flatly denies advice in a relationship where the Bank's own adviser discussed the portfolio is not a defence, it is an exhibit, and it invites the argument that the Bank papered over what it did. The consent structure is better drafting than a disclaimer for the same reason: it names the conflict, records the client's agreement to it, and leaves the Bank's duties in its other capacity where they belong. The saving for duties that cannot be excluded costs the Bank nothing it would have kept anyway and stops an over-broad clause being read down as a whole. The one thing that does not move here is the ability-to-bear-loss acknowledgement, because that is the limb that maps onto the regulators' own question.

ladder.text: Where the Bank or any member of its group provides investment advice or portfolio management to the Borrower or the Pledgor in respect of the portfolio over which security is given, the no-advice representation is limited to the decision to enter into the facility, the amount borrowed and the terms of the facility documents, and does not extend to advice given on the composition or management of the portfolio itself. The sophisticated-investor representation is given as a statement of knowledge and experience relevant to holding a leveraged portfolio of the relevant kind, and the acknowledgement that the Borrower can bear the loss of the entire amount is replaced by an acknowledgement that losses may exceed the cash and other assets deposited and that the Borrower remains liable for any shortfall after realisation. In consideration of those changes, the Bank's records for the facility must include, before the first drawing, a documented assessment of the suitability or appropriateness of the leveraged position as a whole (the facility together with the portfolio it is secured on), completed and retained in accordance with the applicable conduct rules and dated not more than X days before that drawing, and the Borrower and the Pledgor undertake to provide the information the Bank requires for that assessment and to notify the Bank of any material change in the information given. Nothing in this clause affects the Bank's rights on a margin call or on an Event of Default, or imposes on the Bank any duty to notify the Borrower or the Pledgor of an impending or actual collateral shortfall beyond any duty the Bank owes in another capacity or under applicable law.

It swaps a representation the Bank might not be able to rely on for a file the Bank can actually produce: where the relationship is advised, a documented assessment of the leveraged position as a whole is the answer to the conduct question, and a clause is not. The carve-out is drawn narrowly and deliberately - the Bank still says the decision to borrow was the client's, and only gives up the pretence that it said nothing about the portfolio. The last sentence is the part not to trade away: whatever the Bank concedes on advice, the margin and default mechanics stay unconditional, because a duty to warn built into this clause would convert every margin call into a negotiation about whether the warning was adequate.

ladder.text: The Bank will not give, or allow the documents to imply, any representation or acknowledgement that it has recommended the facility, approved the leveraged strategy, or assessed the facility as suitable or appropriate save where a documented assessment has in fact been made and is on file; will not delete the acknowledgement that losses may exceed the amounts deposited, or the acknowledgement that the Borrower remains liable for any shortfall after realisation; will not accept a contractual duty to warn of an impending or actual collateral shortfall, or to advise on the portfolio, in an execution-only relationship; will not make the exercise of any right on a margin call or on an Event of Default conditional on the suitability of the position, on the adequacy of any warning, or on the Bank having given advice; will not accept non-reliance wording which purports to exclude a duty or liability that applicable law does not permit to be excluded, since a clause that overreaches is a clause that may be read down in full; and will not accept a general carve-out from non-reliance for anything the Bank's people may have said, as distinct from a specific written statement the Bank has agreed may be relied on.
ladder.rationale: The line here runs between describing the relationship accurately, which the Bank should always do, and underwriting the client's investment decision, which it must never do. A contractual duty to warn is the clearest example of crossing it: it sounds reasonable in the room, and in a falling market it turns the Bank's right to call and to liquidate into an argument about whether the client was told in time. Note the two limbs that point the other way, and say them out loud because they show the position is not simply one-sided: the Bank will not claim it gave no advice where it did, and it will not exclude what it cannot lawfully exclude. Both are refusals to overreach, and both exist because an over-broad clause is the one most likely to fail when it is finally needed.

clauses.jurisdiction_note: The Luxembourg approach observed in a published template is documentary rather than representational: the facility points at a published investment and risk warning notice and a separate risk disclosure for the more volatile asset classes, then takes a representation that the client has read and accepted them and is aware of the risks, repeated at all times until termination; and it carries a 14 calendar day withdrawal right for a retail client under a distance contract where the facility has not been used (BANK-LU-01). Two practical points follow. The incorporation-by-reference structure means the risk package has to be delivered and its delivery evidenced, which is an operational control rather than a clause. And the withdrawal right has to be identified at intake, because it is a feature of the client's classification and the channel, not of the negotiation. Separately, Luxembourg's consumer credit regime excludes credit granted by a credit institution or investment firm to let an investor carry out a transaction in the relevant financial instruments (LU-CODE-CONSO art. L.224-3), which cuts in the Bank's favour on classification but does nothing for the conduct question this clause is about.

flags.message: The borrower is an individual and no high-net-worth or business-purpose declaration is recorded, so no exemption is made out on the facts the tool holds. In the United Kingdom the exemption logic has sat in the Regulated Activities Order since 1 April 2014 rather than in the Consumer Credit Act 1974: the business-purpose route (art. 60C) needs credit exceeding GBP 25,000 and a wholly or predominantly business purpose, and the high-net-worth route (art. 60H) needs credit exceeding GBP 60,260 or security on land, a prescribed borrower declaration giving up the protections of a regulated agreement, and a compliant statement of net income of at least GBP 150,000 or net assets of at least GBP 500,000 given to the lender before the agreement is made. A Swiss-booked facility usually falls outside the Consumer Credit Act twice over, because Art. 7(1)(b) excludes credit covered by deposited customary bank collateral or by sufficient assets held with the lender and Art. 7(1)(e) excludes credit above CHF 80,000; a Luxembourg-booked facility is outside the consumer credit chapter above EUR 75,000 and again where the credit lets an investor transact in financial instruments.
